CLUB BRUGGE are closing in on new digs.

The Belgian giants have held promising talks with local authorities over securing land for a 40,000-seater stadium.



Construction is due to begin in January.

The Club currently share the Jan Breydel Stadion with Cercle.



It was built in 1975 and houses under 30,000 fans.

Thew new stadium would be built next door in the Sint-Andries district.

Mayor Dirk De Fauw confirmed that outstanding issues had been resolved over the long-term use of the land and approved by the city executive.

Next up, the municipal council will hold a vote before the end of the month in the last stage before the deal is finalised.

Local outlets suggest that FC Bruges will pay £65,000 a year to use the land, but varying reports suggest the term is between 50 and 100 years.

On non-matchdays, public land in the park will be accessible and a new park is being planned around the arena.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The city will create and maintain the area, but litter generated by fans will be the responsibility of the club.

In order to reach a deal, it was agreed that the stadium would include space for tractors and other equipment needed by the city, as well as a staff room.

The £165million project still faces opposition and legal proceedings could yet cause an issue, although construction is not expected to be delayed.

A 2029 completion date has been proposed.

FC Brugges are second in the Pro League with nine wins in 11 matches.



Things are also going well in Europe with three victories in four Champions League outings despite a 3-2 loss to Aston Villa.

Liverpool are travelling to Belgium for a clash on November 25 after taking on Mauricio Pochettino‘s Manchester United on Sunday.

Sports.title: How Pochettino fell in love with Man Utd by watching 1999 Champions League final at Nou Camp with future goalie coach
Sports.content:
Next

MAURICIO POCHETTINO fell in love with Manchester United watching Alex Ferguson pull off the greatest smash-and-grab in Champions League history.

Now 27 years later, the Argentine has got his hands on the keys to a different kind of Old Trafford drama.



The new Old Trafford boss was at the Nou Camp in 1999, cheering on the Red Devils as they ripped Bayern Munich’s hearts out with two dramatic stoppage-time goals to win 2-1.

Sat next to Catalonia-based ­Espanyol team-mate Toni ­Jimenez — now goalkeeping coach at Carrington — Pochettino was swept up in the madness of the comeback.



It secured United an unprecedented Treble after their Premier League and FA Cup triumphs, transformed Ferguson into Sir Alex, made his players legends and turned a 27-year-old Poch into an admirer.

Little did he know that nearly three decades later, he would be the man expected to glue the club back together.

Pochettino said: “In 1999, I was in Barcelona in that final. That was an iconic final, Toni and I were shouting for Manchester United.

“From there, I was so excited to see Manchester United and had more admiration for Sir Alex Ferguson — the best coach in the history of the sport.

“I always admired him and then had the opportunity to meet when I went to Southampton and then we played in Old Trafford in 2013.

“That was a dream come true and then the possibility of meeting him in a restaurant in London.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“That is all the memories I have about that club. Now being a head coach is an honour and a privilege.”

United were seconds from defeat to Bayern when Teddy Sheringham levelled before Ole Gunnar ­Solskjaer landed the ­knockout blow from a second David Beckham corner.

Pochettino said: “That type of game where you stay sitting in your place and you’re so excited.

“It was an amazing game. What happened in the end — it’s impossible not to empathise with that team.



“That made me pay more attention to United, Ferguson and the players who are all legends.”

Ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino, now 54, has spent the best part of ten years flirting with the Old Trafford job, watching the club tumble from one false dawn to another.

With Louis van Gaal’s position in ­jeopardy in May 2016, Ferguson requested to meet then-Spurs boss Pochettino at a London restaurant.

Jose Mourinho was being lined up as Van Gaal’s replacement but that did not stop Fergie asking the League Managers Association secretary for Pochettino’s number.



A lavish two-hour seafood lunch at Scott’s in ­Mayfair might have remained private had ­paparazzi not snapped the pair with Pochettino’s No 2 Jesus Perez outside.

United have since appointed five permanent managers but Poch never disappeared from the conversation.

When Solskjaer was given the caretaker job in December 2018, a league victory over Pochettino’s Tottenham at Wembley the following month was viewed as a positive sign by United.

Two months later, Solskjaer signed a three-year contract.



Quizzed before that meeting almost eight years ago, Pochettino had revealed: “I remember when Ole scored after 90 minutes at the Camp Nou. I was there and shouted for United’s goal.”

Spurs sacked Pochettino in November 2019 — just five months after taking Spurs to the Champions League final.

His availability became an awkward sub-plot to Solskjaer’s reign.

One reason the Norwegian lost the dressing room by November 2021 was his frequent ­references to glory days his players felt so far removed from.



Michael Carrick fell into the same trap, citing Fergie, Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney, Sir Bobby Charlton and Sir Matt Busby during a box office five-minute monologue to open one of his final press conferences.

Nostalgia is no longer accepted as a substitute for success at Old Trafford.

And the club Poch inherits is worlds away from the one that stole his heart in Spain, with United in the relegation places.

He said: “We must start from zero. Culture is the most ­important. We need to create the environment and platform for the players to perform.



“We need to understand the history of the club, try to create a new culture and philosophy that can respect that identity but at the same time, perform.

“If we don’t perform, the responsibility is mine.”

There is no gentle introduction as Poch’s first assignment is a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday.

He has urged his new players to be “fearless” after just ONE Prem victory in ten games, a 5-2 win over newly-promoted Ipswich 82 days ago.



Pochettino’s form as USA boss is in stark contrast to United’s, winning all SIX games since ­losing in the World Cup round of 16 to Belgium, scoring 20 goals and conceding just three.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Red Devils have lost seven of their 15 games this term with their only clean sheet coming against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah FK in September.

United are 18th in the Prem but could be bottom by kick-off on Merseyside if Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win on Saturday.

NEWCASTLE could be ready to end 134 years of history at St James’ Park.

Toon have occupied the famous old stadium since 1892, but their Saudi owners seem to have settled on building a new £1.3billion home over redevelopment.



The Daily Mail claims that club chiefs met representatives from Goldman Sachs this month to discuss funding plans for a 65,000-seater home in Leazes Park.

Newcastle have reportedly conducted surveys around animal and plant life after concerns were raised about the presence of bats in the potential site.



Expanding St James’ is another option, but a new ground is the easiest path to competing with the best clubs in Europe in the age of FFP.

Early designs by KSS architects were compared to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Wanda Metropolitano by those who saw them, per the Mail’s report.

Debts would fall on the club, as opposed to its Saudi backers and a decision could be announced early next year.

Newcastle host Arsenal on Saturday looking to climb the table after a sluggish start.

Under-fire boss Matthias Jaissle revealed that he begged Bruno Guimaraes not to join the Gunners and admitted he hasn’t been able to replace him.

Jaissle said: “I met Bruno really shortly in the pre-season, but the decision was already made from him to join Arsenal.

“I tried my best at least in the end to convince him, but the decision was made.

“I tried to tell him we counted him on as a leader and to explain the role he would have with us. But again the decision was made.

“He informed me. But it’s my job to do my best anyway, and at least I can look in the mirror and say I tried.

“When those conversations started with Newcastle, of course, that was a key player for us, and I hoped until I arrived that he will stay as I was planning with him.

SWANSEA have finally confirmed that Vitor Matos has left the club.

Strasbourg announced the Portuguese manager had taken over on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Arsenal outclassed in defeat to dominant Lyon
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s hopes of automatic qualification to the Women’s Champions League quarter-finals are hanging by a thread after they were beaten 2-0 at home by a dominant Lyon in foggy conditions.

The French side, who beat Arsenal in the semi-finals last season, got the better of the Gunners again at Meadow Park on Thursday night with goals from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay in each half sealing the victory.

Arsenal barely laid a glove on Lyon - who are yet to concede a goal in this season's Champions League - and now sit eighth in the standings, three points adrift of fourth-placed Chelsea, after their first loss in five league phase matches.

Image: Arsenal found it hard to see a way past Lyon in the foggy conditions

Emily Fox registered Arsenal's only shot on target of the game deep in stoppage-time and the home side could easily have conceded a few more had Marie-Antoinette Katoto not spurned two big opportunities.

Arsenal were also indebted to their goalkeeper, Misa, who produced three big saves in the second half to keep out Tabitha Chawinga, Dumornay and Vicki Becho.

Renee Slegers' side, now without a win in three matches in all competitions, are relying on teams above them to drop points in the final round of matches to avoid having to face a play-off match to secure their passage to the quarter-finals.

Meanwhile, Lyon, who currently sit second in the table, have secured a top-four finish with a game to spare after picking up 13 points from five matches.

Slegers: Lyon were better than us

Arsenal Women boss Renee Slegers to ESPN:

"Tough battle. Congratulations to Lyon who were better than us today. They play good football, physically strong in the duels, fast with the ball and without the ball.

"We had a tough time dealing with it in the first half. Second half we controlled the game better without creating clear-cut chances.

"But then you see how clinical Lyon were from their moments."

On her half-time team talk: "It was 1-0, so we were in the game. Like they had, we need moments as well. We are going to get moments and then how we are going to create it."

Analysis: Reality check for Arsenal

Sky Sports News reporter Uma Gurav at Meadow Park:

"The bigger picture here is that Arsenal have played the best two teams in this competition in two consecutive weeks and they've got just one point out of the two games.

"You have to admit the draw was very tough on them to get both Barcelona and Lyon, but it's also a harsh reality check.

"This Arsenal team won the Champions League just 18 months ago. Now, they're not quite up there with the European elites. Can they get back there anytime soon?"

Is it time to question Arsenal boss Slegers?

Ex-Arsenal striker Lianne Sanderson to ESPN:

"I like Renee but there has to come a time [when we question] why is it that all the players look out of form? Apart from Alessia Russo, how many of those players are actually performing?

"There has to come a point where you have to start questioning Renee. As much as I like Renee and everything she's done.

"Not to compare the two, but it feels like Michael Carrick at Man Utd where you feel like someone has taken the team so far but now what?

"We're all waiting for Arsenal to kick on. That tonight disappointed me because it looked flat."

Sports.title: Drone footage of Pochettino's first Man Utd training session leaked online
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session today has been leaked online in a major security breach.

The 12-minute drone footage over their Carrington training ground was uploaded onto YouTube.

It shows Pochettino doing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepare for their clash with Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool

Manchester United Sunday 22nd November 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

United have signs around the Carrington area warning that use of drones are "strictly prohibited" and anyone caught "will be reported for prosecution and subject to civil action".

Image: A "No Drones" sign is pictured outside Manchester United's Carrington Training complex

The uploaders of the drone footage, CC Overview, claimed to have not breached any laws.

On the video they posted: "For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it, the drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.

"The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required.

"As for leaking team news/ tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."

The training today was a closed session and not open to the media.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News.

What do we know about the drone operator? The footage was uploaded to YouTube channel CC Overview

'Colin' describes his channel as 'drone footage mainly of construction at football stadia and events affecting our environment.'

Analysis: Leaked drone footage 'a significant tactical advantage to Liverpool'

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"This 12-minute video starts off innocuously. We see large numbers of Man Utd players on a separate pitch doing what is known as rondos, those small groups of six or seven players with one or two in the middle trying to intercept the ball. It's the classic pre-training warm-up. That's pretty innocuous. That won't give Liverpool or anyone else much of an insight into what Pochettino's tactical thinking might be for his first game in charge.

"But then on the next pitch, as the drone moves across, it zooms in, and the zoom is quite incredible. You can make out faces and we see Pochettino hands-on, walking them through certain match scenarios. At one stage Pochettino calls all those players in for a huddle and a briefing.

Image: Mauricio Pochettino speaking to players on his first day at training as Man Utd boss

"I'm not going to give you any information about who those players are. But these 11 players Pochettino calls in - 10 outfield players and one goalkeeper. We shouldn't assume this is his starting XI, necessarily.

"Saturday would be the day we'd expect United to do their specific tactics and shape to prepare for the game at Anfield the next day. If this was drone footage of that session it would be even more damaging, even more explosive.

"But the fact it's 11 players separated from the group... it's a very difficult situation for Pochettino and Manchester United.

"I don't think [Pochettino and the players] were aware of it at the time.

"It's questionable whether the person handling the drone has done anything illegal. All around Carrington training ground, they have a large numbers of signs up saying drones are prohibited. But it's clear from these images the drone was not flying directly above United's property. It was to the side of United's property and zoomed in.

"There's absolutely no suggestion Liverpool are involved in this, they are clearly not. But you have to say, it could be advantageous to Liverpool and Andoni Iraola if he's planning his tactics for Sunday's game to look at this and get an idea of how Manchester United might be lining up and what Pochettino might be thinking.

"While it seems as though there are probably no laws that have been broken here, nevertheless it's an awful lot of very specific footage which Manchester United and Pochettino would not want out in the public.

"If you look at the impact of what we're talking about, Man Utd earlier today released some images of the training session and it showed Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu among the main training group. Both of those have had injury concerns of late. So those official images told me, Man Utd supporters and Liverpool's tactical preparation experts that Maguire and Dorgu may be in line for possible selection.

"It's gone a stage further now with this leaked drone footage because that has shed even more light on that. It gives a pretty clear picture of who's fit, who's out on the training field, who's involved and who isn't.

"That has to be a significant tactical advantage to Andoni Iraola and Liverpool as they go into this huge game on Sunday."

Watch Liverpool vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Premier League from 4pm on Sunday; kick-off 4.30pm

Sports.title: Nacua handed three-match suspension by NFL for policy violation
Sports.content:
Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy.

The suspension begins immediately and Nacua will be eligible for reinstatement on December 14, following the Rams' Week 14 game against the San Francisco 49ers.

The All-Pro receiver won't be paid during his suspension but, thanks to the timing of his suspension, won't miss any games because he is currently out due to knee and toe injuries.

Nacua went on injured reserve last week and he is eligible to return from both IR and his suspension when the Rams (6-4) host the Dallas Cowboys on December 20.

Image: Nacua is currently sidelined with knee and toe injuries

The Rams and Nacua have been awaiting his probable suspension for nearly a year. The suspension of Nacua stems from an incident on New Year's Eve in 2025, where he allegedly made an antisemitic remark and bit a woman.

The accuser filed a civil lawsuit on March 25 against Nacua for assault and battery, while Nacua's attorney denied his client made any such statements and described the biting as "horseplay."

Nacua entered a holistic care facility earlier that month, before he was sued, the concluded his time in the rehab facility in time to be part of Los Angeles' off-season program in mid-April.

He has appeared in seven games this season, despite battling multiple injuries. He has totalled 70 receptions for 715 yards this season, with four touchdowns.

Nacua also missed two games with a core muscle injury in September before hurting his knee on the final offensive play of the Rams' win at Washington on November 8.

Sports.title: FIA to introduce full-time F1 stewards
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced it will introduce full-time Formula 1 stewards from 2027 with the aim of having "greater consistency in decision-making".

The use of full-time stewards has been a consistent talking point in F1 as different stewards, who adjudicate all racing and technical matters on a race weekend, are used at each event over the season.

There has been an argument that this can lead to inconsistencies in decision-making when it comes to imposing penalties, or the severity of a penalty.

But the FIA announced on Thursday, ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, they will begin to recruit full-time stewards with a phased introduction from next year with the aim of establishing 12-15 full-time stewards over the coming years.

Currently, there are four stewards drawn from a large FIA pool of officials and one of those is a former racing driver. The new structure will continue to use the knowledge of driver stewards at each event and the FIA say full-time stewards will "allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making".

The news comes a month after the opening of the FIA Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill in the UK, following a reorganisation of Race Control in 2022 after the controversial 2021 season which saw Max Verstappen overtake Lewis Hamilton on the last lap of the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Image: The "significant financial turnaround" under FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem's has helped create the full-time stewards programme

"This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport," said FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.

"The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport.

"Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships."

Sports.title: Mardle: The Worlds is now the 'incentive' for Littler
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Darts' Wayne Mardle believes Luke Littler has to use winning the World Darts Championship as his motivation following his Grand Slam of Darts loss; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22

The World Darts Championship is now the 'incentive' for Luke Littler after Grand Slam of Darts loss, says Wayne Mardle

Wayne Mardle says he doesn't know how Luke Littler will feel ahead of the World Championship, after crashing out of the Grand Slam of Darts

Luke Littler suffered a shock 10-8 defeat to Jermaine Wattimena at the last 16 stage of the Grand Slam of Darts and Sky Sports Darts' Wayne Mardle believes the world No 1 now has to throw all his energy into being ready for the World Darts Championship.

Littler was attempting to become the third player ever to win the Wolverhampton event three times in a row alongside Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen.

However, he came up against an incredible performance from Wattimena, in which he was hitting T20s for fun and averaged over 101.

With Littler also missing the Players Championship, which is the last major before Alexandra Palace in December, the next time we will see Littler on the TV stage is when he plays his opening Worlds match on Friday December 11 as the reigning champion, live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the second-round match between Luke Littler and Jermaine Wattimena at the Grand Slam of Darts

Littler went into 2026 targeting a clean sweep of majors and while he won the Premier League, Masters, UK Open, and World Matchplay, his loss in the second round at the World Series Finals to Dirk van Duijvenbode has started a run without a major win.

He has since not defended his World Grand Prix title, Grand Slam title, or clinched the European Championship, which has eluded him.

For Mardle, Littler has to put everything else to one side, use his time away to get fresh, practice, and win the major that just has something a bit different to the rest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler is out of the Grand Slam of Darts after being beaten by Jermaine Wattimena in round two

"There is no doubt that every player gets more motivated. The Worlds is different," Mardle said.

"The run-up is different and the build-up to it is gigantic.

"He went basically nine months into the year holding this belief and everyone else thinking he's going to do the clean sweep.

"So it was nine months of all this and then it ends, but the Worlds is out on its own. The incentive is that it is the Worlds. That is all the incentive you need. It is the biggest and it is the best event.

"If he loses in that then he will have gone four months without a major.

"The Worlds is the one, and Michael van Gerwen said this for years: what is the point in winning anything else? You only need to win this one.

"I think that is just the same with Luke's mentality."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler sent Sky Sports commentators Wayne Mardle and Dan Dawson wild with his audacious three-bullseye checkout

'You are better winning the Players Championship'

The talk has already turned to whether Littler's time away from the TV spotlight will be a positive or a negative as he attempts to become the second player ever, alongside Taylor, to have won the World Darts Championship three or more times in a row.

Mardle insists that, while it would be better for Littler to be heading into the Worlds as a potential Players Championship winner after his loss at the Grand Slam, if he brings his A-game, it is his to lose.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Incredible scenes in Wolverhampton as Luke Littler appeared to ask his team if he should go for three bullseyes, then duly delivered on the incredible 150 checkout!

"I don't know how he really feels about losing here at the Grand Slam but what I do think going forward, because he's not playing in the Players Championship, so his next outing will be at the Worlds.

"This is the way that I would frame it - would he be better not playing, or would he be better winning the Players Championship? You are better winning the Players Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player John Part and Mark Webster try to recreate Luke Littler's triple bull finish from the Grand Slam of Darts

"But that is the kind of situation that you don't know. You don't know if he goes to the Players Championship, wins it or loses.

"If he loses, it is like maybe he shouldn't have gone to that, in hindsight and everything else.

"I really believe for Luke, if he can turn up fresh, if he can turn up ready, if he can turn up with anywhere near his A-game, he probably wins the Worlds again. That will be three times on the bounce by the age of 20, which is ridiculous."

'It reminds me of trying to beat Taylor'

Wattimena picked up the biggest win of his career against Littler at the Grand Slam but it is not the first time he has come out on top against 'The Nuke' as he beat him in August on the way to winning a Players Championship title.

Wattimena said that win gave him confidence and reinforced that Littler is "not a robot" and Mardle believes that win can be credited for the performance we saw from the Dutchman in the Grand Slam.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Jermaine Wattimena gives his reaction to his win over Luke Littler at the Grand Slam of Darts

"I know this is a thing. I was about when Phil Taylor was hardly ever beaten and until you actually beat him, you don't believe you can," he said.

"You see others beat him, there were loads throughout the years. There was Andy Callaby. Adrian Gray beat him. There were others that beat him that were not as good as me.

"I remember thinking why can't I ever beat Phil? It is not until you do that you know that someone's not a robot.

"So that win was massive for Jermaine and it was one of the reasons why he won yesterday.

"Now going forward after yesterday, he can beat anyone on that stage. Luke Humphries has to watch out if he plays Jermaine. Gerwyn Price, they should all watch out now.

"It is really important to have belief. Now he has got it and he has got the ability."

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Fulham ideal visitors for flagging City

After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. Simon Burnton

Manchester City v Fulham, Saturday 12.30pm (all times GMT)

2 Villa seek to end tough winless run

Positivity surrounds Aston Villa despite them failing to win in four matches, the last of which ended in agonising fashion; they had to settle for a 4-4 draw at Manchester United after twice squandering a two-goal advantage. Villa should have managed the final minutes better, but a home date with Sunderland presents an opportunity to return to winning ways. Unai Emery needs to eliminate the defensive naivety that has blighted some performances and the expected absence of Matty Cash, this time owing to concussion sustained on Poland duty, would deny the Villa manager his preferred defensive lineup. This fixture threw up a classic last season, Tammy Abraham scoring a stoppage-time winner to extend the visitors’ miserable record at Villa Park. Sunderland have won on only two of their past 17 league visits, their last victory coming in 2011 courtesy of the former Villa loanee Phil Bardsley. Ben Fisher

Aston Villa v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen John McGinn scores at Manchester United but Aston Villa’s positive performance went unrewarded. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Ed Sykes/Apl/Sportsphoto

3 Scott return keeps Cherries sweet

The last time Alex Scott played for Bournemouth, Marco Rose was yet to taste victory in the Premier League. When the 23-year-old returns to midfield he will do so with the team in a totally different place. Bournemouth have racked up eight straight wins in all competitions before hosting Nottingham Forest on Saturday and Scott, who has been able to build his fitness during the international break after a thigh problem, may have to wait his turn owing to the form of Tyler Adams and Ryan Christie. If Rose opts for momentum, then Eli Junior Kroupi, fresh from scoring his first France goal, could make his first start of the season after sustaining a freak foot injury in pre-season. Bournemouth have hardly been short of firepower, though, with Evanilson scoring seven goals in his past eight games. BF

Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

4 Will Chelsea front up to Calvert-Lewin?

Chelsea left Wearside battered and bruised after being pushed around by Brian Brobbey. The Sunderland forward bullied Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill, who had to be substituted at half-time, and won the game’s decisive penalty with a solo run that left Xabi Alonso angry with his side’s powderpuff defending. Alonso insisted Chelsea had prepared for Brobbey’s threat; the Chelsea manager will hope they are better at putting the plan into practice when they face another target man on Saturday. Leeds head to Stamford Bridge and will look to Dominic Calvert-Lewin, fresh from helping England get over the line against Spain last weekend, to unnerve Alonso’s defenders. Jacob Steinberg

Chelsea v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

5 Set pieces key at Frank’s Palace bow

Thomas Frank’s first assessment of his new charges after taking over at Crystal Palace this week included the nuggets that “we’re conceding too many goals … we need to work on the defensive side of things with principles, attitude, everything regarding that”, and in particular “we need to work on the set pieces, that’s key”. If he can’t inspire an immediate improvement this is where this match could be decided, being as it is an encounter between the league’s worst set-piece defenders – no one comes close to the 67 shots and xG of 7.44 coughed up by Palace at restarts – and the best. Though Coventry have let in one goal from set pieces, and neither Brentford nor Liverpool have shipped any, the hosts’ set-piece xG of 1.65 is a league low, and they were equally outstanding from dead-ball situations in the Championship last season. The home side will be boosted by the return of the 6ft 4in defender Bobby Thomas, who, despite a calf injury that meant he missed the last two games and the final third of the one before that, has still made more clearances than any other Coventry player. SB

Coventry v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Thomas Frank wants his new Crystal Palace charges to tighten up at set pieces. Photograph: John Walton/PA

6 De Zerbi is only show in town for Spurs

It may have been a slightly strange week for Tottenham fans. They have watched as their former managers Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank have been installed at Manchester United and Crystal Palace respectively, while their current head coach, Roberto De Zerbi, picked up the Premier League’s manager of the month award for October. That is reflective of the improvement De Zerbi has overseen in recent weeks, with Spurs happy to move forward with the Italian and avoid the chaos enveloping some of their rivals. The long-held assumption among some connected to Tottenham that Pochettino would one day return to save the club must now be banished; De Zerbi needs full buy-in from everyone to build his project. That’s the only way Spurs can ensure they steer clear of future crises. Dominic Booth

Tottenham v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

7 Frosty reception awaits Guimarães

With the temperature in Newcastle forecast to dip to 0C at kick-off, Matthias Jaissle is perhaps hoping that his team’s guests from north London (where a balmy 9C is predicted at 5.30pm) freeze in the Tyneside chill. Otherwise it is hard to envisage his young side overcoming a formidable looking Arsenal on a day when Newcastle’s head coach seeks what would be only his second win in seven games. Home fans will not merely be hurt by the sight of their much-missed former captain Bruno Guimarães wearing Arsenal colours but decidedly nervous about a fixture that precedes a run of tricky engagements involving a trip to Brighton and home dates with Manchester United and Sunderland. Jaissle’s cause could be helped should Mikel Arteta name Guimarães in his starting XI and the crowd respond to the once adored Brazilian’s defection by creating the sort of hostile atmosphere that might just galvanise a Newcastle team expected to contain the former Arsenal midfielder Joe Willock. Meanwhile Jaissle’s defence must be mindful of the threat posed by another Newcastle old boy in Mikel Merino. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Arsenal, Saturday 5.30pm

8 Brighton must handle favourites tag

Brighton are out to prove their early-season form has been no fluke and the fixture list for November and December looks promising for their chances of retaining their lofty position. Hull, having started the season with back-to-back league victories, now appear vulnerable and have not won since that August burst. Brighton follow the trip to Humberside with a home game against Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League, then host Newcastle, and face none of the big six until a visit to Tottenham on 29 December. With Brighton having won seven of their 10 league games, tentative talk of a title challenge may not seem so fanciful come Christmas. The challenge tactically for Fabian Hürzeler’s men will be to deal with the tag of favourites for most of their upcoming games, with teams perhaps starting to wise up to Brighton’s high-pressing, vertical style. DB

Hull v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross celebrates scoring against Brentford to help extend Brighton’s excellent form. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

9 Pochettino looks to set tone at Anfield

And so it starts all over again. Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager in 13 years – not forgetting the interim spells of Ryan Giggs, Michael Carrick, Ralf Rangnick and Darren Fletcher – was impressively quick to commit to the cause when taking a private jet from Cincinnati to Manchester immediately after his final game as USA head coach. Mauricio Pochettino needs his new, floundering team to reciprocate at Anfield. United have conceded four times in the first four minutes of a game this season, seven goals in the opening 17 minutes in total, and will have had little time to absorb instructions from their latest coach by the time they face an expectant Liverpool. United’s defensive options might tempt many managers to board the next flight out but, as a decent record against the so-called big six since the start of last season demonstrates, the team are capable of showing up when they feel like it. That is just one of the many issues Pochettino has to address. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Manchester United, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Brentford relish Pawson patrol

Fans of neutral officiating will appreciate the fact that both Brentford and Everton have won six games refereed by Craig Pawson, who will take charge of this match. But where the two clubs’ experiences diverge is that, while Brentford have only danced to the tune of the Pawson whistle 12 times, enjoying a 50% win ratio, Everton have toiled through 33 Pawson-helmed matches for an equivalent figure of 18%. Of Everton’s past 14 Pawson-patrolled matches there has been only one victory, and 10 defeats. Pawson, meanwhile, has taken charge of five Brentford home matches and they have won every one, thanks in part to the two penalties he has awarded them (both converted), compared with the one he gave against them (missed). Jack Grealish is back having sat out Everton’s past four league games because of illness, lack of fitness and a breach of club discipline, but given that, of the three Premier League matches he has missed, Everton won the two most recent – and the other one was at Arsenal – he may not go straight back into the team. Indeed of Everton’s four league wins this season, Grealish has missed three and played only eight minutes in a fourth. SB

Sports.title: OL Lyonnes show their class to hit Arsenal’s ambitions for a top-four WCL finish
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes, as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.

Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the ­difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are joint-top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.

It feels like Lyonnes are playing with a fire and intensity fuelled by their loss to Barcelona in May’s Champions League final. They look a more formidable, coherent and hungry side on a mission to end a four-year run without lifting the trophy they won eight times in a 12-year period between 2011 and 2022.

“We are already at a better level for sure,” said the Lyonnes manager ­Jonatan Giráldez. “Sometimes you just need time. We had nine new ­players last season and I was new too as the coach. I think we have improved the rhythm of the game and have identified positions better and are staying more compact. The most important thing is speaking the same language in possession and out possession.”

The visit of the eight-time ­European champions was always going to be challenging for the ­Gunners and based on current form getting a result would be even tougher. Last season’s runners-up had scored 20 goals without conceding in their first four Champions League matches prior to their trip to Borehamwood and scored 49 in their nine Première Ligue games.

The lack of competitiveness in the France top flight also meant they were able to rotate heavily at the weekend between their two European games. Giráldez made 11 changes for their 1-0 defeat of Saint-Malo on Saturday before returning to his first-choice lineup against the 2025 Champions League winners.

Quick Guide Women's Champions League: Pina hat-trick fires brilliant Barça to top spot Show Clàudia Pina scored a hat-trick as Barcelona thrashed Servette 6-0 to go top of the Women’s Champions League standings. While Lyon were winning 2-0 at Arsenal, Barça edged clear at the top on goal difference as they dismantled their Swiss visitors. Aitana Bonmatí fired in the opener in the 19th minute and then turned provider for Pina to drill home her first goal. Esmee Brugts headed in a third in the 32nd minute, and Barça had their fourth just after the hour, with Caroline Graham Hansen hitting an emphatic penalty after Bénédicte Simon fouled Brugts. Pina got her second in the 77th minute and tucked in from Brugts’s pull-back to complete her hat-trick late on. Bayern Munich are two points behind after cruising to a 4-0 win over Austria Vienna. Klara Buhl headed the visitors in front after 27 minutes before Pernille Harder doubled the lead in first-half stoppage time. Alara Sehitler’s stunning strike made it 3-0 with 15 minutes to go before Sophie Proost added a fourth in stoppage time. Sofia Jahnukainen struck in stoppage time as Roma snatched a 3-2 win away to Benfica. Kayleigh van Dooren twice put the Italians in front, but her first goal was cancelled out by a thunderbolt from Caroline Møller, with Flourish Sabastine equalising after her second. Paris FC got their first win of the competition, beating HB Køge 2-1 thanks to Célina Ould Hocine’s late penalty. Catherine Paulson fired the visitors in front 10 minutes in, but Sheika Scott bundled in a rebound to bring Paris level before the break. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal were not afforded the ­luxury of an easy league match after their battling 1-1 draw against ­Barcelona last week, playing a critical and tricky game against London City Lionesses, which also ended 1-1. Renée Slegers made two changes to the team that hosted ambitious London City, with Ona Batlle ­having picked up a knock Taylor Hinds played at left-back and Kyra Cooney-Cross started ahead of Kim Little.

They had their backs against the wall at a bitterly cold Meadow Park, as Giráldez’s galacticos controlled the game. The away team had almost 69% possession in the first half and amassed 12 shots to Arsenal’s one.

View image in fullscreen Melchie Dumornay doubles OL Lyonnes’ lead in the second half. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

The surprise was that Lyonnes were not further ahead at the break, with Brand’s 24th-minute goal the difference, the full-back sweeping in Vicki Bècho’s ball from the right.

Brand was back to haunt the ­Gunners, having scored in both legs of last season’s semi-final between the two teams, with the French side progressing to face Barcelona in the final with a 4-3 aggregate win.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal were better after the break, but Lyonnes soaked up brief spells of Arsenal pressure, Marie-Antoinette Katoto the only player left forward as they banked back and crowded the box to give the home players few options.

They increased their margin and dampened the mood soon after Arsenal’s brightest period, Tabitha Chawinga’s cross from the left was collected by Katoto and the France forward laid the ball off for Dumornay who took a touch before powering the ball into the roof of the net.

It was an emphatic and unstoppable finish from one of the best players in the world as a mist lowered over the pitch.

“Congratulations to Lyonnes, they were better than us today,” said Slegers. “If you look at the block we’ve had, the challenges we’ve had with the run of games – ­Liverpool and Barcelona away, ­London City who are among one of the top teams in the WSL right now and Lyon, who are even better than last year – it’s a lot of games against strong teams with a short turnaround because Lyon were better than us.”

Arsenal need to quickly move on, with West Ham their last game before the international break. They had needed a win to have any serious chance of earning a place in top four, avoiding a quarter-final playoff place.

They now sit eighth and will face Inter in their final league phase match in December, with the Italians needing a win to keep any hopes of a playoff place alive. That will not be easy, but a seeded playoff place is in Arsenal’s hands, if they want it.

Sports.title: England get one-match suspended ban on away tickets for anti-pope chants in Spain
Sports.content:
England have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain. The punishment is suspended for two years.

Uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid. A further charge in the next two years could trigger a ban on away fans for a competitive game.

In a statement given to the Mail, the FA said: “We will not ­tolerate this unacceptable and deeply ­offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all ­England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.”

Uefa’s control, ­ethics and ­disciplinary body announced that it had decided “to fine the English ­Football ­Association €15,000 and to order against the ­English Football Association a full ­restriction on selling tickets to its ­supporters for one representative team competition away match, for the ­racist and/or discriminatory ­behaviour of its supporters.

“Said full restriction on selling tickets to supporters for one away match is suspended for a ­probationary period of two years, starting from the date of the present decision.”

The relevant article of Uefa’s disciplinary regulations reads: “If one or more of a member association or club’s supporters engage in the behaviour described in paragraph 1 [insulting the human dignity of a person or group of persons on whatever grounds, including skin colour, race, religion, ethnic origin, gender or ­sexual orientation], the ­member association or club ­responsible incurs a minimum of a fine and either a ­partial stadium closure or a ­restriction on selling tickets to its supporters for away matches.”

Quick Guide How do I 

The match had been preceded by Thomas Tuchel reminding his players of the anti-­racism protocols, given the last match between the sides in Madrid, in 2004, had notoriously been marred by abuse aimed at England’s black players.

Last month Spain were fined £15,000 and ordered to play their next friendly with a partial stadium closure after discriminatory chants about Muslims during March’s match against Egypt in Barcelona.

Sunday’s chant is a staple for some England fans but sung relatively rarely in stadiums. Several more frequently heard chants target only the IRA, including inserting “No surrender” into the national anthem.

Sports.title: Fifa sparks tension with demand for tax-free status in UK for Women’s World Cup
Sports.content:
Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four football associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The UK bid to host the tournament is due to be ratified at an extraordinary Fifa congress in Zurich on Monday and the Guardian has learned there is tension behind the scenes over many of Fifa’s requirements, which multiple sources involved in the discussions have indicated will not be met.

Fifa is understood to have requested blanket exemptions on tax for all football-related activities for it and its broadcast and commercial partners, as well as its suppliers and staff. It also wants ticket sales – projected to reach 4.5m for the 48-team competition – to be VAT-free and for currency exchange fees to be waived.

Government sources have told the Guardian such blanket exemptions will not be granted for financial reasons and the optics of giving tax breaks to Fifa, which has cash reserves of more than $4bn (£3bn).

Fifa’s governance crisis has also complicated matters, with the prime minister, Andy Burnham, having called on the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, to resign on multiple occasions, and the FA preparing to endorse France’s Philippe Diallo at March’s presidential election.

Negotiations involving Fifa, the Treasury and the domestic FAs will continue after the UK bid has been ratified. Some carve-outs may be granted but the government is adamant the World Cup will not receive the wholesale tax-free status Fifa is seeking.

An FA spokesperson said: “We provided every guarantee that we can provide under the laws of the country and flagged any deviations transparently. Our approach is also consistent with every major event the UK has hosted or is due to host, including London 2012 and Euro 2028.”

Fifa identified in its evaluation report of the bid the UK’s tax and legal framework as a “medium risk” for the tournament, which would need to be addressed.

Fifa’s tax requirements have proved challenging for many tournament hosts in recent years, including last summer’s men’s World Cup. After months of negotiations with the US Treasury, Fifa succeeded in securing a late exemption from federal taxes for the 48 competing teams, although many were forced to pay state and city tax on their World Cup earnings depending on the location of their matches.

The tax adviser Oriana Morrison, who has worked for many national associations, said: “Fifa will ask for the world but ultimately accept the minimum that enables the tournament to be commercially viable. There are likely to be some difficult conversations ahead as the tournament will not generate anywhere near as much money as the men’s World Cup, so the margins are far tighter.”

A government spokesperson said: “Hosting the Fifa Women’s World Cup 2035 would be a major opportunity for the UK, delivering a significant economic boost to communities across the country and helping drive a decade of change in women’s sport.

“Government guarantees are an important part of any bid for a major event on this scale and we have engaged with Fifa throughout the process to ensure a proportionate approach. We are now looking forward to Monday’s hosting decision.”

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino calls for Manchester United to show no fear against Liverpool
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

“We are going to Anfield with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United,” Pochettino told the club’s website. “The history talks for us, and what we need to expect. We need to be sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday after an overnight flight, having taken charge of his final USA match against Haiti. He toured the training ground and held meetings with senior staff and players not on international duty.

Members of Pochettino’s staff were in place earlier in the week as they seek to revitalise a team with one league win. Pochettino is waiting for United to ratify the appointment of Sílvia Tuyà, a strength and conditioning coach who worked with him with the USA. She travelled with him by private jet to Manchester but was not named among the staff later in the day.

“We need to go little by little, step by step,” Pochettino said. “We cannot go too fast but also we need to, at the same time, attack the priorities to build something.”

He said it was important he and his staff adapt to the culture of the club. “And then, with this sense of knowing the history of the club, try to create all together, because we are all different, a culture, a philosophy that can respect that identity, the history of the club. But at the same time, performing. If we don’t perform, the responsibility is mine.”

Pochettino has coveted the United job and is a keen admirer of Sir Alex Ferguson, whom he describes as “the best coach in history”. Since the Scot’s retirement in 2013, United have failed to match his success but Pochettino said he was looking at “the potential of the club”. The weight of past achievements has hindered individuals over the past 13 years.

“The players need to express their talent,” Pochettino said. “We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now: it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He sounded an upbeat note, saying: “With the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

United’s total borrowings have risen to £784.5m, with long-term debt up by almost £100m over the past year. Figures published for the three months to 30 September show long-term borrowings of £577.4m, compared with £481.2m 12 months earlier. United’s cash reserves fell from £80.5m to £55.5m during the same period despite an increase in revenue.

The club reported a quarterly net loss of £18.1m, compared with £6.6m ​in ​the same period a year earlier. Revenue rose by 4% to £146m.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs vote through new rules to increase legal protection for board
Sports.content:
Clubs rallied behind the Premier League’s leadership in a key vote on Thursday, overwhelmingly backing new rules that would protect the chief executive, Richard Masters, from potentially damaging lawsuits.

A vote to expand the legal indemnity afforded to Premier League directors was won 18-2 at a shareholders’ meeting in central London, granting Masters and other figures greater protection in the event they were subjected to legal action as a consequence of doing their job.

Manchester City are understood to be one of two clubs to vote against the extension of indemnity, and one unnamed side spoke out at length against the measures during the meeting. The other vote against was by Nottingham Forest, who felt insufficient time had been granted to consider the proposal.

The rule change follows reports that the organisation’s leadership may be named in possible legal action by City’s Abu Dhabi sponsors, who have claimed their reputations were damaged as a result of the excoriating verdict of an independent commission regarding City’s breaches of the league’s financial rules. City have appealed against the verdict.

This week the Abu Dhabi telecommunications giant and City sponsor Etisalat released a statement describing the contents of the verdict as “entirely false and defamatory”. Referring to the independent commission’s report as “the published findings of the English Premier League”, Etisalat said it was “actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter”.

The details of any increase of indemnity, including who would cover any potential costs, were not discussed in the meeting.

The chief refereeing officer of Pro Ref, Howard Webb, attended and came under sustained questioning from club executives over recent referee and video assistant referee failures.

A report by the independent key match incidents panel this week found there had been two serious mistakes that were not corrected by the VAR during the most recent round of matches. Webb is understood to have acknowledged that performance in matchday 10 had been “poor” but argued that apart from that weekend, key metrics on decision-making had been trending in the right direction this season.
