World.title: Zamfara govt inaugurates committee to review salary structure for tertiary institutions
World.content:
The Zamfara State Government has inaugurated a committee to review and address the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare issues in the state-owned tertiary institutions.

The Secretary to the State Government and Chairman of the Committee, Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee and chaired its maiden meeting on Thursday in Gusau, the state capital.

The committee is expected to examine relevant government circulars towards addressing all outstanding welfare concerns of staff in the institutions.

It will also determine financial implications and funding requirements involved, and consult relevant stakeholders to facilitate amicable resolution.

Speaking at the inauguration, Mr Nakwada reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to staff welfare, industrial harmony, and the repositioning of tertiary education in the state.

He further emphasised that Governor Lawal has proven to be workers-friendly, citing the upward review of the minimum wage from paltry N7,000 to N70,000, the clearing of the backlog of gratuities, implementing new salary scale for healthcare workers, and other welfare commitments of the current administration.

“This assignment is a clear demonstration of Governor Lawal’s commitment to the welfare of workers, industrial harmony, and the development of our tertiary institutions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The demands presented by the Forum of Zamfara State Tertiary Institutions (FOZASTI) and the Zamfara State University on salary, allowances and promotion benefits have been a source of concern. The government considers it necessary to address these issues holistically, fairly and sustainably.

“Our assignment must be guided by objectivity, sincerity, and the best interest of the State. We must listen to all parties, examine the facts and figures dispassionately, and come up with recommendations that are implementable, affordable and just.

“I assure the staff unions and management of our institutions that this Government is not unmindful of their plight. At the same time, we must also be mindful of the financial realities of the State.

“Our goal is to find a lasting solution that will guarantee industrial peace and improve the quality of education in Zamfara State,” the SSG stated.

Mr Nakwada further appealed for patience and understanding as the government works gradually but deliberately to address staff welfare concerns, stressing that while not all issues can be resolved at once, every legitimate demand is being given the attention it deserves.

He urged aggrieved unions to give dialogue a chance and allow the committee to complete its assignment, noting that industrial action at this critical moment would only hurt but not help the system.

Members of the Committee include the Commissioners for Finance, Education, Science and Technology, Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, and Budget and Planning.

Other members are Special Adviser on Economic and Financial Matters, the Representatives of the Forum of Tertiary Institutions, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Zamfara State Chapter, and Zamfara State University, while the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, serves as Secretary.

World.title: 2027: Uba Sani targets 70% Kaduna votes for Tinubu
World.content:
Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) will mobilise voters to secure 70 per cent of votes cast in the state for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election.

Sani stated this on Thursday during the inauguration of the Kaduna State APC Governorship Campaign Council, where he expressed confidence in the party’s chances in the forthcoming elections.

He said the massive turnout at the event demonstrated the level of support the APC enjoyed in the state.

“The massive crowd that turned out today demonstrates the level of support our people have for our party and the confidence they have in our leadership,” he said.

The governor said Kaduna would reciprocate the support President Tinubu had given the state through his administration, particularly in infrastructure, healthcare, education and security.

“The level of support our government and the people of Kaduna State have received from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is unprecedented in the history of our country,” he said.

He added that Tinubu had supported the state in addressing insecurity and providing infrastructure and other critical interventions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the Federal Government approved four federal universities for Kaduna State, although the state initially requested two.

He listed the institutions as the Federal University of Education, Federal University of Applied Sciences in Kachia, Federal University of Plant Science and Federal University of Technology.

Sani also mentioned some road projects requested from the Federal Government, including Manchok-Bakin Bayi, Zaria-Soba-Pantsega and Jema’a-Gwantu roads.

He said the state had also requested the construction of a light rail project to improve transportation and connectivity.

The governor further said the Federal Government had approved N20 billion in development support for the state, while students had benefited from more than N6 billion in scholarships and other educational assistance.

On security, Sani said several communities that previously faced accessibility challenges due to insecurity had recorded improvements.

“When President Tinubu assumed office, several local government areas and communities were facing serious accessibility challenges because of insecurity. Today, every local government area in our state is accessible,” he said.

He, however, acknowledged that security remained a work in progress, mentioning Birnin Gwari, Giwa, Kajuru, Chikun and Kagarko among areas where improvements had been recorded.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, who is the second vice-chairman of the campaign council’s Advisory Council, charged members to work for total victory for Tinubu and Sani.

Abbas described the inauguration as the beginning of a strategic political assignment, urging members of the council’s 41 directorates to translate their appointments into concrete electoral results.

“Every office must have a target, every target must have a timetable. Every timetable must end at the polling unit. Organisation wins elections. Discipline protects victory. Unity delivers the mandate,” he said.

He urged the council to extend its mobilisation activities to all 23 local government areas, wards and polling units, while assisting eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards.

Abbas also called for greater involvement of women and youths in campaign leadership and urged the party to engage traditional and religious leaders, workers, farmers, traders and persons with disabilities.

He said the APC should campaign on its achievements rather than promises, citing federal investments in education, healthcare and transportation.

The Speaker commended Sani for prioritising rural development through investments in roads, schools and primary healthcare facilities.

He also cited the reopening of markets and the return of farmers to their farmlands in parts of Giwa and Birnin Gwari as signs of improving security.

World.title: Rivers-born businessman, Kelechukwu Dimkpa speaks on public confusion over his identity
World.content:
Rivers State-born architect, international businessman, lecturer, philanthropist and Architect, Kelechukwu Dimkpa, has expressed concern over repeated cases of mistaken identity involving him and Mr Seyi Tinubu, son of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Dimkpa said the perceived striking physical resemblance to the president’s son has repeatedly attracted unexpected attention from members ofthe public in Nigeria and abroad.

According to him, the encounters occur at airports, on flights, in marketplaces, public places and even during business engagements, where strangers approach him believing he is Seyi Tinubu.

He explained that some of those who mistake him for the President’s son go as far as presenting personal challenges, requesting financial assistance and seeking interventions, apparently believing that he has direct access to the Presidency.

The architect said the situation has become increasingly uncomfortable, particularly when some individuals refuse to accept his explanation that he is not Seyi Tinubu or his twin brother.

Dimkpa described the experience as an unusual challenge that has affected his everyday public engagements.

He said the mistaken identity has occurred both within and outside Nigeria, with some people approaching him excitedly at airports and other public places, convinced that they have encountered a member of the President’s family.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Despite the recurring incidents, Dimkpa said he has built his own professional and business career, with interests spanning Nigeria, the United States, China, and a lot more.

He stressed that he is an entirely different individual with his own family background, professional accomplishments and personal responsibilities.

Dimkpa hails from Adanta in Isiokpo, Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State, South-South Nigeria. He is a Consulting Director at Smart City Engineering and Construction Limited.

He attended the Rivers State University, Rivers State, Academy of Art University in San Francisco, California, and Morgan State University in Maryland, United States, where he pursued his academic and professional development.

His international exposure has influenced his business interests, which extend beyond architecture to international trade, industrial equipments, construction machinery and commercial transportation.

The businessman also maintains commercial relationships in China, particularly in Xi’an City, where his activities include sourcing and supplying oilfield tools, heavy-duty trucks and other industrial products.

He is equally involved in Building transportation systems.

Beyond his commercial activities, Dimkpa is also involved in philanthropy, mentorship , widows and youth empowerment.

According to information about his philanthropic engagements, he has contributed to the training and development of more than 100 individuals, students not left out through initiatives aimed at improving their skills and economic opportunities.

His philanthropic interests reflect his belief in using entrepreneurship and personal resources to create opportunities for others.

Despite the inconvenience associated with the repeated cases of mistaken identity, Dimkpa maintains that he has respect and admiration for Seyi Tinubu.

He said he has no intention of exploiting their perceived physical resemblance or presenting himself as the President’s son.

Rather, he wants members of the public to recognise him by his actual identity and respect his personal space.

For the Rivers-born architect, the recurring experience has become a reminder of the unexpected challenges that can arise when an individual may bear a striking resemblance to a prominent public figure.

He maintains that while the resemblance may attract curiosity, it should not be a reason for people to disregard his identity.

“Dimkpa recently received an award at the 7th Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe Annual Award Lecture in recognition of his contributions to nation-building.”

World.title: Court remands accountant over alleged N60m fraud
World.content:
A state high court in Benin, Edo State, on Thursday, ordered the remand of Victor Osayamen, a former accountant with Uyi Technical Limited, to a correctional facility over alleged N60 million fraud.

Mr Osayamen faces four counts of stealing. He pleaded not guilty when the charges were read out to him.

Counsel for the defendant, I. O. Obare, made an oral application for his client’s bail.

Olayinwola Afolabi (SAN), the counsel for the nominal complainant and Chief Executive Officer of Uyi Technical Limited, Uyi Oloton, did not oppose the application.

However, the judge, Rita Irele-Ifijeh, declined the oral bail application.

Justice Irele-Ifijeh directed the defence counsel to file a formal written bail application, scheduled for hearing on 27 November. She also ordered that witness summons be issued.

The judge subsequently adjourned the case to 21 January 2027 for hearing.

World.title: AMR: Pharmacist urges Nigeria to implement policies to curb drug resistance
World.content:
Nigeria needs to translate its antimicrobial resistance (AMR) policies into action to curb the growing threat of drug-resistant infections, a pharmacist has said.

Folashade Lawal, managing director and chief executive officer of Victory Drugs, said the country had developed policies and guidelines to address AMR but faced challenges implementing them across healthcare facilities and communities.

“The challenge now lies not in planning but in implementation,” Ms Lawal said on Thursday while delivering the ninth Ladipo Mobolaji Abisogun-Afodu Annual Lecture in Pharmacy at the College of Medicine, University of Lagos.

The lecture, titled Addressing Antimicrobial Stewardship in Nigeria: Current Perspectives and Future Imperatives, was held during the 2026 World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, observed from 18 to 24 November.

Policies, implementation gaps

Nigeria’s first National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance covered 2017 to 2022. The plan sought to reduce, prevent and slow the emergence of resistant organisms through awareness, surveillance, infection prevention and control, responsible antimicrobial use, and research.

An assessment of its implementation found that only 44 per cent of the plan’s activities had been completed, highlighting gaps in coordination, funding and implementation across sectors.

Nigeria subsequently launched its second One Health National Action Plan on AMR, covering 2024 to 2028, with six strategic objectives, including stronger governance, surveillance, public awareness, infection prevention and control, responsible antimicrobial use, and research and capacity development.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Lawal said antimicrobial stewardship activities are yet to become routine in many healthcare institutions, despite the country’s policy commitments.

She called for stronger enforcement of regulations governing antimicrobial sales, sustainable funding for stewardship programmes at federal, state and institutional levels, improved access to diagnostic services and laboratory infrastructure, and the establishment of stewardship programmes across healthcare facilities.

She also urged the government to strengthen antimicrobial consumption monitoring, invest in workforce development and research, and expand public awareness of responsible antimicrobial use.

In his welcome remarks, the Dean of the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Lagos, Sunday Adesegun, said antimicrobial resistance threatened the effective treatment of infectious diseases and could reverse gains made in modern medicine.

He said Nigeria continued to grapple with self-medication, indiscriminate access to antibiotics, inadequate infection prevention and control, and gaps in antimicrobial resistance surveillance.

“Antimicrobial stewardship is not merely a professional responsibility; it is a collective obligation to safeguard public health,” Mr Adesegun said, urging stakeholders to move beyond awareness to concrete action.

Growing threat

Ms Lawal described antimicrobial resistance as a “silent pandemic” that steadily undermines the effectiveness of medicines used to treat infections.

She said bacterial antimicrobial resistance was associated with approximately 4.7 million deaths globally in 2021, including 1.14 million deaths directly attributable to resistant infections.

In Nigeria, she cited estimates that antimicrobial resistance was directly responsible for 50,500 deaths and associated with about 227,000 deaths in 2021.

She warned that resistance threatens not only the treatment of common infections but also modern medical procedures, including surgery, cancer treatment, organ transplantation, neonatal care and intensive care, which depend on effective antimicrobials.

Ms Lawal identified self-medication, inappropriate prescribing and dispensing, unrestricted access to antibiotics, weak regulatory enforcement, inadequate infection prevention and control, and limited diagnostic capacity as major drivers of antimicrobial resistance.

She said inadequate laboratory services often leave healthcare professionals relying on empirical treatment without diagnostic confirmation.

Pharmacists’ role

Ms Lawal urged community pharmacists to refuse inappropriate antibiotic supply without valid prescriptions, source medicines from regulated suppliers, counsel patients on proper use and refer patients for medical care when necessary.

She said hospital pharmacists should support stewardship through prescription reviews, monitoring antimicrobial consumption and collaborating with other healthcare professionals to optimise treatment.

She also called for antimicrobial stewardship to be integrated into pharmacy education and for stronger collaboration among healthcare professionals.

The chairman of the occasion, Olumide Akintayo, a former president of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria, said healthcare professionals, government and other stakeholders had contributed to inappropriate antimicrobial use.

He called for urgent action, including improved regulation, public awareness and responsible professional practice.

He also noted that Nigeria would host the fifth Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on Antimicrobial Resistance in December.

Research grant

At the event, Olusegun Ajala of the Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Lagos, won the 2026 Ladipo Mobolaji Abisogun-Afodu Research Grant Award in Pharmacy and received N2.7 million.

His proposal, titled Development of a Psidium guajava-Based Antibiotic Adjuvant for Restoring the Susceptibility of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria to Conventional Antibiotics, was selected as the winning research proposal.

Deborah Ogundemuren and colleagues from the Department of Pharmaceutics and Pharmaceutical Technology came second with a proposal to develop a bioactive, sprayable hydrogel for postpartum perineal wound care as an antibiotic-sparing strategy.

Osideko Oluwaseun and colleagues from the Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry came third with a proposal on the chemical standardisation and antibacterial characterisation of fermented maize mash supernatant, known as omidun, produced using different fermentation strategies.

World.title: From Corporate Responsibility to Community Impact: LG Electronics expands clean water initiative
World.content:
LG Electronics is strengthening its Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) commitment through its solar-powered borehole initiative, providing access to clean water for more than 20 communities across Nigeria.

The initiative reflects the company’s dedication to improving everyday living through sustainable technology and community-focused investments. By providing solar-powered water infrastructure, LG Electronics is helping underserved communities address water access challenges while reducing dependence on conventional electricity supply.

Speaking on the company’s commitment to community development, Mr Paul Mba, Head of Corporate Marketing, LG Electronics Nigeria, emphasised that innovation must deliver meaningful benefits beyond consumer products.

Mba explained that the company’s responsibility extends to identifying practical ways its technology and resources can improve lives within the communities it serves.

Recent interventions in Kaduna and Ondo States further demonstrate the national reach of the programme, which combines renewable energy, community participation and social investment to support sustainable development.

Through this growing initiative, LG Electronics continues to demonstrate that corporate responsibility is most meaningful when it translates into tangible benefits for people and communities.

World.title: APC in Ebonyi rejects ‘rainbow coalition’, says state is entirely APC
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council in Ebonyi State has rejected the existence of a proposed rainbow coalition in the state, insisting that such a political arrangement does not exist.

The Chairman of the council’s Media Directorate, Emmanuel Onwe, made the declaration on Thursday during a media briefing in Abakaliki.

Mr Onwe said the council would not discuss the coalition while focusing on Governor Francis Nwifuru’s re-election campaign.

He said the council’s director-general had reiterated the governor’s position that no rainbow coalition existed in Ebonyi.

“Ebonyi is entirely APC, as all members of the State Executive Council and the 24 members of the State House of Assembly are members of the party.

“All elected senators, members of the House of Representatives, local government chairmen and appointed officials are APC members,” he said.

However, Mr Onwe acknowledged the right of other political parties and groups to pursue their political interests through lawful democratic activities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Democracy allows individuals and groups to carry out activities in pursuance of their political interests, but such must be done within the confines of the law.

“Our duty, however, is to propagate the good works of the governor and the reasons he should be re-elected for a second term in office,” he said.

He also pledged that the APC and the state government would not condone violence, lawlessness or extra-judicial acts during political activities.

“We would promote the ideals and good works of the government, as I advise those who have grievances to report such to security agencies.

“The state government and the APC would not protect anyone found culpable in any unruly act,” he said.

Mr Onwe, a former commissioner for information and orientation in the state, said the council would conduct its campaign with honour and integrity.

World.title: Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has said the ongoing redevelopment of the Obalende Bus Park, known as the Y’ello Bus Park, will be completed and ready for public use by the end of December 2026.

The facility, being developed by MTN Nigeria as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, is designed to accommodate more than 1,000 buses.

Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Obalende project and another MTN-sponsored under-bridge recreational park at Falomo, Ikoyi.

Wahab, who was accompanied by key government officials, including the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, Sola Giwa; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Adekunle Akodu; General Manager of the Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency (LASPARK), Adetoun Popoola; and Director of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, said the six-week completion window was agreed upon after consultations with stakeholders to resolve operational challenges.

He explained that the project was initially scheduled for completion within 21 weeks following an inspection of the area by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his deputy as part of efforts to transform the previously degraded environment into a modern transport hub.

However, construction was delayed by logistical challenges involving existing transport operators conducting business at the site.

Wahab said the government had engaged the transport unions, contractors and the Special Adviser on Transportation to agree on temporarily relocating operators from the immediate construction area to enable the contractors to complete the work.

“Today was just to see how far they’ve gone. Thankfully, they had one or two logistics issues that had to do with the businesses that have been operating there, legacy things like the transport business.

“We had to engage the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, the transport unions, and the contractors to see how we can give them a space for a maximum of six weeks—not shutting the place down 100 per cent, but moving them out of that immediate workspace to enable the contractors to complete it and hand it over to them to operate,” he said.

The upgraded facility is designed to accommodate approximately 1,000 buses and will feature dedicated parking and loading bays, sleeping facilities for drivers, modern toilet facilities and green areas.

The design also incorporates collapsible barriers along the perimeter to allow drainage maintenance teams access to the adjoining canal for regular cleaning and maintenance.

Addressing concerns about possible commercialisation of the facility and increases in transport fares, Giwa assured commuters and commercial transport operators that access to the terminal would be free.

“No, there’s no toll at all. It is for them; they are the ones using it. We are just making it a standard park that we will replicate all over the state as time goes on,” he said.

On the management of the facility after completion, Giwa said it would remain the property of the Lagos State Government under the supervision of the Ministry of Transportation.

He added that the government was working with transport unions to ensure effective utilisation of the facility and prevent its takeover by miscreants.

Giwa also warned commercial bus drivers against picking up passengers or parking along road corridors outside the designated terminal after its opening.

He said the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) would enforce compliance with traffic regulations.

“By the time we finish this place, there will be no need for us to have any bus on the road, and Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, will be on the ground to ensure they comply with all the rules and regulations of Lagos State.

“The laws are there. No one is above the law. We have provided the park for you, and if you come out of that park to obstruct traffic, definitely the law will take its course,” he warned.

Falomo under-bridge gets recreational park

Following the inspection at Obalende, the delegation visited the Falomo under-bridge, where MTN is also transforming a previously degraded space into a recreational park for public use.

Speaking at the site, LASPARK General Manager, Popoola, said the area, which was previously characterised by indiscriminate waste dumping and misuse, was being reclaimed as a relaxation centre for residents.

She said the facility would follow the model of the JJT Park in Alausa and remain open to the public free of charge for everyday recreational activities.

However, corporate organisations and other groups seeking to organise formal events or competitions at the venue would be required to pay a nominal maintenance fee, she added.

The Obalende project was formally handed over to MTN Nigeria by the Lagos State Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources on April 15, 2026, with an initial 21-week completion target.

The September 11 deadline was missed following delays attributed to heavy rainfall between June and August and operational challenges involving existing park management.

Construction resumed in mid-October, with clearing, foundation work and material deliveries, while interlocking pavement, curbing and fencing works were ongoing as of mid-November.

The wider redevelopment plan also includes electric vehicle charging points, more than 60 public toilet fixtures, a recycling drop-off station, kiosks and commercial spaces, solar lighting and tree planting.

Other components include a Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) road camp for street sweepers and security personnel, improved lighting and CCTV facilities, as well as maintenance arrangements for the park and adjoining Macgregor Canal.

World.title: UNIZIK VC urges 19,522 graduands to uphold discipline, excellence
World.content:
UNIZIK

By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA – The Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Stanley Anyaehie, has urged the 2025 and 2026 graduating students of the institution to uphold its core values of discipline, excellence and self-reliance as they begin the next phase of their lives.

Anyaehie gave the charge on Thursday in Awka while delivering his address at the university’s 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies.

He urged the graduands to become worthy ambassadors of the institution, named after Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, popularly known as Zik of Africa.

Expounding on the university’s motto, the Vice-Chancellor said discipline required the graduands to make integrity, self-control and ethical conduct their guiding principles in an increasingly complex world.

On self-reliance, he advised them not to wait for opportunities to come their way but to embrace innovation, create value, build enterprises and develop solutions to real-life challenges.

He also urged them to pursue excellence and reject mediocrity, stressing that every task they undertook should reflect world-class standards.

Reflecting on his tenure as the institution’s seventh Vice-Chancellor, Anyaehie reaffirmed his commitment to scholarship, clinical integrity, effective higher education governance, staff development and institutional transformation.

He said his administration’s philosophy, “A Greater UNIZIK is Possible,” was not merely a slogan but a commitment to repositioning the university as a globally competitive centre of academic excellence, technological innovation and societal impact.

Presenting the convocation statistics, the Vice-Chancellor disclosed that a total of 19,522 graduands would receive various qualifications, comprising 16,260 first-degree recipients and 3,262 postgraduate graduands.

Of the first-degree recipients, 213 graduated with First Class Honours, 4,623 obtained Second Class Honours (Upper Division), 8,751 earned Second Class Honours (Lower Division), while 2,116 graduated with Third Class Honours and 71 obtained Pass degrees.

Another 486 students received unclassified degrees in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences.

The postgraduate category comprised 701 Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) recipients, 35 Master of Philosophy/Doctor of Philosophy (MPhil/PhD) recipients, 1,224 master’s degree recipients, 323 Postgraduate Diploma (PGD) recipients and 979 Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE-NTI) recipients.

Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Anyaehie said institutional reforms had been implemented to strengthen academic standards, improve staff welfare, expand the university’s capacity and modernise its operations.

He also identified the full re-accreditation of the university’s Medical programme by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) as a major milestone in its academic and professional development.

In his remarks, the Chancellor of the university, His Royal Majesty, Da Jacob Gyang Buba, CON, Gbong Gwom Jos, acknowledged the presence of dignitaries and graduating students and extended greetings to President Bola Tinubu.

He paid tribute to the institution’s founding inspiration, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, describing his legacy as an enduring source of inspiration.

The Chancellor also appreciated the Federal Government, Federal Ministry of Education, National Universities Commission (NUC), benefactors and friends of the university for their financial, infrastructural and moral support.

Similarly, the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Barr. Monsur Olugbenga Kukoyi, congratulated the graduating students, describing the convocation as a celebration of perseverance, character and scholarship rather than merely a university tradition.

World.title: Ogun polytechnic students protest ASUP strike, seek Abiodun’s intervention
World.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

ABEOKUTA — Students of state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State on Thursday protested at the Governor’s Office, Oke Mosan, Abeokuta, demanding Governor Dapo Abiodun’s urgent intervention to end the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP).

The protest, organised by hundreds of students under the aegis of the National Association of Polytechnic Students (NAPS), followed the expiration of two separate 48-hour ultimatums issued to the government without what the students described as concrete action towards resolving the dispute.

The strike, which has kept students out of classrooms for about 10 days, has disrupted academic activities across the six state-owned polytechnics.

Armed with placards bearing inscriptions such as “Gov. Dapo Abiodun, please end ASUP strike”, “Save Polytechnic Education Now”, “Our Lecturers Must Return to the Classroom” and “Attend to Our Lecturers’ Demands”, the protesters urged the governor to intervene personally and ensure an immediate resolution of the crisis.

Speaking during the demonstration, the Chairman of NAPS, Ogun State Liaison Council, Comrade Joshua Opatunmibi, said the students had exhausted available diplomatic channels and could no longer remain silent while their academic future was being jeopardised.

He explained that the protest was not intended to confront the state government but to draw attention to the hardship caused by the prolonged strike and demand decisive action.

Opatunmibi said the students had made several appeals to the government and issued two 48-hour ultimatums without the desired response.

He said: “On November 12, we issued a 48-hour ultimatum to the state government, appealing to Governor Dapo Abiodun to urgently intervene and bring an end to the ongoing ASUP strike.

“The 48 hours elapsed without any meaningful action from the government. Consequently, on Monday, we addressed another press conference, appealing to the government to come to our rescue because the strike had stalled our education. We also issued another 48-hour ultimatum.

“That ultimatum expired on Wednesday afternoon, but we were disappointed that nothing had been done to address our concerns. We are really unhappy. Does it mean that the government does not care about our plight?

“The closure of all the polytechnics in the state is seriously affecting us. We cannot continue to sit at home while our academic programmes and future plans are being put on hold.

“We are here to demonstrate that the voices of students matter. We are not fighting the government; we are simply demanding that the issues responsible for this strike be resolved.

“We cannot continue to put our future in jeopardy. We appeal to Governor Abiodun to please attend to the demands of our lecturers so that we can return to our respective institutions and complete our education.”

Also speaking, a NAPS member, Kolade Musbau, expressed disappointment over what he described as the government’s lack of urgency in resolving the dispute, saying students were bearing the brunt of the industrial action.

Musbau lamented that students who should be attending lectures and progressing with their academic programmes had been forced to remain at home, threatening their ability to complete their studies within the stipulated period.

He said: “The students are not happy that, instead of being in school, we are at home wasting valuable time because of this ASUP strike. Despite our repeated appeals, it appears that the government is not ready to do the needful.

“We have, therefore, been left with no option but to embark on this protest to draw the government’s attention to our plight and demand urgent intervention to end the strike.

“We are all eager to return to our respective institutions and complete our studies within the expected period. We appeal to Governor Abiodun to bring this strike to an end without further delay.”

Responding on behalf of the state government, the Permanent Secretary, Bureau of Cabinet and Special Services, Mr Dolamu Idowu-Agida, assured the protesters that the government was making efforts to resolve the disagreement with the lecturers.

Idowu-Agida disclosed that the government had held two meetings with relevant stakeholders to address the issues surrounding the industrial action.

He also revealed that approval had been granted for an increase in the monthly subvention to all state-owned polytechnics, expressing optimism that the strike would be called off within 48 hours.

He said: “I want to assure you that the state government has held meetings with relevant stakeholders on this matter twice. The government is seriously addressing your concerns.

“As of yesterday, approval had been granted for an increase in the subvention to all the polytechnics in the state.

“The issues raised by your lecturers are receiving serious consideration. I want to assure you that the matter will soon be resolved and your lecturers will return to the classrooms.

“Be rest assured that your lecturers should be back in the classrooms within the next 48 hours.”

It will be recalled that lecturers in the six state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State embarked on an indefinite strike last Wednesday following the expiration of a 15-day ultimatum issued to the state government to address their outstanding demands.

The industrial action followed the alleged non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA), as well as concerns over what the union described as inadequate funding of the institutions.

ASUP had also faulted the government’s continued payment of a monthly subvention of N5 million to some of the state-owned polytechnics, arguing that the amount had remained unchanged for more than a decade despite prevailing economic realities and rising operational costs.

Among its major demands, the union is seeking payment of outstanding CATA and EAA entitlements, as well as an immediate review and upward adjustment of the monthly subvention to N100 million for all state-owned polytechnics.

The union maintained that increased funding was necessary to meet the institutions’ operational needs, improve the quality of education and ensure effective delivery of academic programmes.

World.title: Trial of killers of Ademola, Salami begins in Lagos
World.content:
By Innocent Anaba

THE long-awaited trial of four persons accused of the alleged murder of Prince Akinloye Ademola and Sherriff Ishola Salami in the Ajiran area of Lagos State commenced yesterday, with the Lagos State prosecution opening its case before the court.



The trial began before Justice A. Muyideen of the Lagos State High Court sitting in Igbosere.Those standing trial are Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo; Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga; Tajudeen Ahmed, aka Ahmed Ajiran; and Bode Ajose.



The prosecution team was led by the Lagos State Solicitor-General, Mr Adebayo Haroon, while the defence counsel included Mr O. Ajanaku, Mr R. Owolabi, Mr Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and Mr Gbenga Ojo, who represented the third defendant. Mr M. Familola represented the fourth defendant.



The prosecution called its first witness, ASP Nosiru Isiaka, a police officer attached to Special Squad 1 of the Lagos State Police Command, who testified on the circumstances surrounding the investigation and eventual arrest of the defendants.



In his evidence-in-chief, ASP Isiaka narrated how the police initially arrested the first two suspects, Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo, and Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga, and how the third suspect was later arrested through the technical team from the Inspector-General of Police’s office in the Ajiran area of Ajah.

He further told the court how investigations eventually led to the arrest of the third defendant. He was about to narrate how the investigation led to the arrest of the fourth suspect, Mr Ahmed Tajudeen, when his testimony was interrupted by the defence counsel. The police witness, while recounting the investigative steps taken by his team, explained how information obtained during the investigation helped the police establish links between the four defendants and the alleged murder of the two victims.

However, proceedings were interrupted by objections from the defence counsel, Ojo, SAN, and the other three lawyers representing the defendants, who challenged the manner in which the prosecution witness was presenting his evidence.

Ojo, who is the leading counsel to the defendants, argued that the police Investigating Police Officer (IPO), being the first prosecution witness, could not give evidence.

in a manner suggesting that he personally witnessed the circumstances surrounding the killings when, in fact, he was only an investigating officer who was not present at the scene of the alleged crime.

He maintained that the witness must confine his testimony to facts within his personal knowledge and properly distinguish between what he personally did or observed during the investigation and information allegedly obtained from other persons in the course of police inquiries.

The objection interrupted the proceedings as the defence sought to ensure that the prosecution’s evidence remained within the boundaries of admissible evidence under the law.

Further hearing in the matter has been adjourned until November 25.

World.title: Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm
World.content:
By Matthew Johnson

The Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria, SOFPON, yesterday raised the alarm over the state of primary healthcare in the country, revealing that only about 20 per cent of more than 30,000 Primary Healthcare Centres ,PHCs, nationwide are fully functional.

Vice-President of SOFPON, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu, who disclosed this during a press conference themed, “Primary Health Care Without Family Physicians: Can Nigeria Afford the Gap?”, will also focus on “The Double Burden of Disease and the Cost of Fragmented Care” and “The Stressed Family Physician and Continuity of Care”. on November 19th 2026 ahead of the society’s 29th Annual General and Scientific Meeting ,AGSM, said the country’s primary healthcare system was facing a serious operational crisis.

He explained that the shortage of skilled medical personnel, poor funding and increasing migration of doctors were undermining access to quality healthcare, calling on the Federal Government and state governors to urgently integrate family physicians into the leadership of primary healthcare facilities.

Yakubu who said the majority of PHCs were unable to provide essential medical services due to structural decay, inadequate funding and shortage of skilled health professionals.

According to him, the conference will develop policy and clinical recommendations on integrating specialist services into primary healthcare, improving physician welfare and retention, and developing integrated care models for infectious and chronic diseases.

He described the situation was being worsened by the increasing migration of doctors, particularly frontline medical professionals, due to poor working conditions, inadequate equipment and weak welfare structures.

He said loss or sidelining of family physicians could further weaken the country’s healthcare delivery system, particularly at the grassroots where continuous and comprehensive medical care is required.

He further explained that family physicians were specially trained to manage patients holistically, coordinate treatment and address both infectious and chronic diseases at the primary healthcare level.

Yakubu said the country’s healthcare system was battling a double burden of disease, with communicable illnesses such as malaria, tuberculosis and cholera existing alongside rising cases of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, kidney diseases and cancer.

He warned that the absence of coordinated healthcare services was increasing treatment costs for families and making it difficult to manage patients with multiple health conditions.

He said the society also urged governments to move beyond constructing PHC buildings to adequately equipping existing facilities and providing sufficient funding and personnel to operate them.

Yakubu added that positioning family physicians at the centre of primary healthcare would promote early detection of chronic illnesses, reduce treatment costs and ensure continuity of care.

He said: “Data shows that only about 20 per cent of the over 30,000 PHC facilities across Nigeria are fully functional, with a vast majority unable to provide essential medical services.

“The rest suffer from structural decay, severe funding deficits that fall far below the 15 per cent Abuja Declaration target, and a devastating shortage of skilled medical professionals.

“When you remove the Family Physician, the specialist trained specifically to manage multi-dimensional, continuous, and holistic patient care from the community level, you create an unfillable gap.

“We are here today to tell the government and the public that Nigeria cannot afford this gap. Fragmented care is too expensive, too dangerous, and completely unsustainable,” he said.

“The society also raised concerns over the welfare of doctors, warning that excessive patient workloads, burnout, economic pressures and security threats were affecting the quality and continuity of healthcare delivery. A single family doctor in Nigeria today routinely consults for numbers of patients that far exceed international safety standards.

“Why does the stress of a doctor matter to the average Nigerian citizen? It matters because a stressed doctor is a direct threat to the continuity of care. If we want a healthy nation, we must care for the people who care for the sick. A broken doctor cannot heal a broken healthcare system.

“Against this backdrop, SOFPON called on the Federal Ministry of Health, state governors and health sector administrators to make the integration of certified family physicians into the administrative and clinical leadership of primary healthcare authorities mandatory.

“I further called for targeted rural allowances and improved security measures for doctors working in underserved and high-risk communities.” Yakubu said.

SOFPON said the issues would form part of discussions at the 29th AGSM, where family physicians, medical scholars and policymakers would examine strategies for strengthening primary healthcare delivery.

World.title: Afreximbank provides $30 m to finance Nigerian SME exports through NEXIM
World.content:
Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs).

The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM).

“The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement issued toay.

The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said.

It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos.

“Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets. This US$30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying.

“By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added.

Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said,

“We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This US$30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.”

The Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) is Afreximbank’s flagship programme for Africa’s creative and cultural industries. It supports the development of commercially sustainable, export-ready creative businesses through access to finance, skills, markets, commercial partnerships and policy support.

CANEX WKND 2026 took place from 5 to 8 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural & Creative Arts in Lagos. Organised by Afreximbank, hosted by the Government of Nigeria and delivered in partnership with the African Union Commission and the AfCFTA Secretariat, it brought together creatives, investors, buyers and policymakers from Africa, the Caribbean and the diaspora.

NEXIM is Nigeria’s export credit agency and is owned equally by the Ministry of Finance Incorporated and the Central Bank of Nigeria.

World.title: Korea sees Nigeria as gateway for K-Beauty in Africa – Deputy Head of Mission, Tak Namgung
World.content:
By Nkiruka Nnorom

Tak Namgung is the Deputy Head of Mission at the Korean Embassy in Abuja. He spoke to journalists on the sidelines of the Korea-Nigeria joint seminar at the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos.

Let us start with K-beauty. Your Ambassador spoke briefly about collaboration in that field. He said in the short term, K-beauty in Nigeria will mainly be about trade. What does that mean in practice?

In the short term, it is about trade and expanding the market here in Nigeria.



I recently spoke with fellow Korean diplomats who came to Lagos a month ago. They are based in Gabon, Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire. We share the same goal of promoting Korean beauty products. They told me they have a very strong chain — those trading in Gabon also have a network in Côte d’Ivoire, and a very strong branch in France. They are all connected.



As some of you mentioned, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is important. When we see its full implementation, Nigeria will be a bridge, a gateway for all products.



After speaking with my colleagues, I felt I must work harder to have a stronger market presence here in Nigeria, because they see more productivity and more profit in our neighbouring, front-running countries.



That is what the Korean Embassy is doing right now. We know consumers deserve genuine products, without counterfeits. Proper registration will help them rely on local distributors. There are strong online customers. They are the ones in desperate need, so that they can have strong confidence in great products. And that opens the way for Korean manufacturers to come to Nigeria for production.

The Ambassador also spoke about shea butter. How does that fit in?

We spoke quite a lot about shea nuts. About 40 per cent of all shea nuts are produced here in Nigeria, but only about 1 per cent of the global shea market actually comes to Nigeria.



Nigeria is heading to fill that gap. NIIA serves as a wonderful platform for such conversations. It provides the intellectual discourse between the Korean Embassy, the Korean government, and Nigerian authorities that will eventually contribute to policy, and also to the business side, for Korean business persons to come.



There is a good example. As was said during the presentation, we will have Beauty West Africa in Lagos. There will be a Korean pavilion, and we will present K-beauty products.

What would Korea gain from this collaboration?

Today we held a seminar on cultural cooperation, in collaboration with NIIA. From here, we navigated the possible cultural collaboration.



According to the data, Nigeria’s creative economy accounts for about 2.3 per cent of the GDP. Nigeria also expects, by 2030, to create 2 million jobs from the creative economy. So it gives more opportunities for Korea as well.



Korea and Nigeria already have strong collaboration. For instance, we have had two joint dramas. One in 2024, titled My Sunshine, and this year, we also have My Alien Lover. That is the outcome of the collaboration between Korea and Nigeria. It is in Korean, English and Yoruba. So it shows a clear example of how our cultural collaboration is well maintained.

Can you tell us about Korea’s cultural success and what Nigeria can learn from it?

I would say Korea and Nigeria both have their unique cultures. It is about how both countries can have the opportunity to see each other. I am not saying this as a matter of capability or something. It is just a matter of time for Nigeria to flourish when it comes to cultural expansion.



But what I would like to point out is that we need collaboration. With its unique culture, Korea also has some platforms to make use of. And Nigeria has the core culture that needs to be promoted across the world.

What key steps is the Korean government taking to strengthen its cultural relationship with Nigeria?

I would like to highlight K-beauty as one of the potential collaboration points. This November, we will have a K-beauty showcase and conference here in Lagos. And in two weeks, we will also have Beauty West Africa, also held in Lagos. We will have a Korean pavilion.



So this is the first step we would like to take for Nigerians to enjoy Korean beauty products. But we also look forward to future collaboration in the near future because Nigeria has a large share in shea nut production. I also see it as an opportunity for potential collaboration in the field of cosmetics industry.

One of the presenters mentioned cultural exchange between Korean and Nigerian artists. Is this something you are looking at?

Yes. Fortunately, we do have a platform in place. We have the Korea Cultural Centre Nigeria, which was established in 2010. Now it is 2026, so it has been working for 16, 17 years.



We also have the Korean scholarship programme, which brings an average of 10 Nigerian university students and others to Korea. And we also have the KOICA scholarship programme. KOICA is Korea’s development agency. We also have scholarships through it.



With that human exchange, we expect — and the main point is — that they do not stay in Korea after graduation. They come back to Nigeria, and with affection for Korea, they come back to Nigeria and they become at the forefront in promoting cultural collaboration between the two countries.

There is a Korean cultural centre here in Abuja. Is there a Nigerian art/cultural centre in Korea? Is it possible to have one, just like we have one here?

I don’t think there is. It is at the discretion of the Nigerian authorities. But I think at least the conditions are already in place. Having an institution is important, but I would say the ambition I see here in Nigeria and also in Korea is already well in place.



For instance, as I said during my speech, we recently had in Seoul the Seoul Africa Festival. There was a Nigerian performer who has been inspired by both Korean and Nigerian culture. He had a mixture of K-pop and Afrobeats. So, it also shows a clear example of how our culture can be assimilated and appeal to the general public in the world.

World.title: Africa must be co-investor, not aid recipient, in proposed GECF gas bank — Expert
World.content:
By Nkiruka Nnorom

African countries must enter the proposed Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) gas bank as co-investors and strategic partners, rather than mere aid recipients, an energy policy expert has said.

Energy policy, markets and regulation consultant, Ifey Ikoneu, made the call at the conclusion of the Eighth Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, while assessing key directions of Russian-African energy cooperation.

Assessing the initiative to create a gas bank, Ikoneu described it as very good, but warned that its success would depend directly on a balance of interests.

“It is important that this does not become just another multilateral investment institution where Africa’s interests are not put first,” she said.

According to her, African countries should act not merely as recipients of funds, but as co-investors and full participants in strategic decision-making.

Ikoneu said the bank should not only finance export infrastructure, but also the continent’s domestic needs, including electrification, petrochemicals, fertilizer production and industrial development, even given that many such projects are traditionally considered non-bankable.

For the new structure to work effectively, she said it would need transparency, protection from political interference and coordination with the African Development Bank, Afreximbank and Africa Finance Corporation.

She stressed that the continent’s domestic needs are extremely acute despite its wealth of energy resources with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without access to electricity.

In this context, she said the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline — a project long stalled due to financing problems — takes on particular significance.

Ikoenu noted that launching it requires a strong institutional framework among Nigeria, Niger and Algeria. At the same time, the pipeline should serve not only as an export channel to Europe but also as a driver of industrialisation for the participating countries.

This, according to her, applies especially to Niger, which is critically dependent on imported electricity and costly diesel generators. An infrastructure union, she said, will allow the three countries to collectively defend their interests on the export market, while giving Russia the opportunity to act as a strategic partner both in the construction itself and in training the necessary personnel.

Touching on the principle of technological neutrality enshrined in the GECF Moscow Declaration, the expert called for interpreting it as broadly as possible.

“This should mean not just a choice between imported technologies, but also the freedom to develop one’s own,” she said.

Ikoneu proposed creating a joint Russian-African research and innovation centre in the gas sector, expanding scholarship programmes for African students in Russia, and more actively involving women in the energy sector.

The main priority, she said, is investment in African specialists and institutions capable of building their own industrial competencies.

She emphasised the crucial role of the GECF as a platform for South-South cooperation among developing countries, saying that the Forum gives gas producers the opportunity to coordinate actions, ensure market transparency and shape fair pricing through long-term contracts.

“A fair global gas market is not only one that guarantees supplies to consumers, but also one where resource-owning countries have a fair opportunity to benefit from them,” she explained.

She warned that the value of such collective action by developing countries is especially high against the backdrop of current geopolitics.

As the expert warned, “sanctions against one country can hit commercial agreements with another state that is not involved in the sanctions confrontation at all,” she said.

World.title: Outbound International Passenger Traffic Declines on Economic Downturn, High Airfares
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chinedu Eze

The reduction in the number of Nigerians who travel abroad has been attributed to the decline in economic opportunities in Europe, coupled with the stringent visa policies and high cost of travel.

Also, there is a growing number of Nigerians who are returning to invest in the country in line with the current movement of foreigners returning to invest in Africa.

Reports have shown that international travel and mobility for Nigerians have faced increased constraints and shifts in 2026 due to tightening visa restrictions, soaring travel costs, and reduced passport accessibility.

Recently, the IziVisa Passport Ranking Index placed the Nigerian passport at 181st globally, showing a drop in pure visa-free destinations from 44 down to 24, as countries like Tanzania, Uganda, Cambodia, and others reclassified entry requirements.

US and Western visa constraints, alongside shifting policies, have created major hurdles for new visitors, students, and immigrant applicants, steering many travellers to look elsewhere.

Also, high exchange rates and expensive flight tickets, have made traditional long-haul trips to Europe and North America less accessible for many middle-class Nigerians.

A country manager to one of the foreign airlines operating in Nigeria, told THISDAY that ticket prices have increased and that the addition of $23 dollars round trip to each passenger ticket introduced by the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) in partnership with the Ministry of Interior’s Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) has further increased the cost of tickets.

Reports also showed that in response to high costs and Western visa bottlenecks, Nigerians are now pivoting to intra-African travel—benefiting from more liberal visa policies in countries like Rwanda, Kenya, Benin Republic, and Ghana.

Reports also confirmed that there is a direct and strong connection between stricter global visa restrictions and the lower rate of international travel among Nigerians

Major destinations have severely tightened access. For example, US travel and visa restrictions introduced in 2026 partially suspended or slowed tourist, student, and immigrant visas, shifting visitor visas to shorter, single-entry terms. Similarly, countries like Canada and the UK have cut down study permits and tightened immigration/sponsorship criteria.

Due to these heavy crackdowns in North America and Europe, many Nigerian travellers are re-routing toward more welcoming African destinations with visa-free or simplified entry policies, such as Kenya, Rwanda, and Egypt.

However, travel expert and organiser of Akwaaba African Travel Market, Ambassador Ikechi Uko, told THISDAY that visa restriction would not affect those who have been obtaining visas in the past.

He confirmed that there were diminishing job opportunities in the West: Europe, the United States and Canada. He also confirmed that there was increased cost of travelling because the price of flight tickets has gone up.

Uko said that there was high demand for jobs few years ago cross the West because they wanted care givers and some countries liberalized their visa policies to attract more people to work.

According to him, after the COVID-19, there was increase in the quest to travel to Europe and North America because these countries have aged population and they were in desperate need for care givers.

“But this demand has saturated. It is not that it has stopped. After COVID-19, more people were hired because of their aged population. There was influx of care givers to Europe and North America in 2022 and 2023. There was an increase in the people who japaed from Nigeria to Manchester and Canada because of the high demand of caregiver services there,” he said.

But the International Air Transport Association (IATA) has indicated that African carriers have recorded strong year-on-year international passenger demand growth throughput in 2026, consistently outperforming the global average.

IATA projected that overall African air travel demand would grow by six per cent for the full year 2026, outpacing the global traffic growth projection of 2.1 per cent to 4.9 per cent depending on the outlook revision.

In 2025, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) reported almost five million international passenger traffic, including inbound and outbound movement.

Also, in 2025, data from the Billings and Settlement Plan (BSP) of the International Air Transport Association, disclosed that foreign airlines and domestic operators on international service, raked in about $1.1 billion in 2025, adding that most of the passengers were on outbound flights.

Record also confirmed that Nigerians continued to travel for many essential factors. According to the record, for outbound and inbound to strike a balance, government must carry out studies to know the factors that make Nigerians leave the country.

For several years, international flights have recorded more outbound flights.

Investigations revealed that finding jobs in Canada, and the United States has become much harder for Nigerians and other international applicants due to a mix of tightening immigration rules, shrinking entry-level and graduate job markets, and a global shift toward skills-based hiring

Reports stated that destinations like the UK, entry-level and graduate vacancies have dropped sharply (with graduate openings falling significantly over recent years), driven partly by economic pressures and the rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and automation in retail, customer service, and corporate support roles.

Also, Western governments have dialed back or restructured post-study work routes, family reunification, and general work visas. For example, policy shifts and tighter vetting in the US and Europe have increased scrutiny on foreign applicants and reduced sponsorship appetite from employers.

Another factor is that many Nigerian professionals move abroad with academic degrees or local experience that do not automatically translate to foreign licensing standards. Western markets heavily prioritise localised technical certifications, digital competencies, and hands-end experience over paper qualifications, leaving many underemployed upon arrival.

However, Business Insider Africa has reported that Nigerians abroad were expanding their support for their homeland, moving beyond remittances to investing in and building businesses across Africa.

THISDAY also confirmed that some Nigerians married to foreigners were returning to live permanently in Nigeria with their families and also some African-American were also returning to motherland to live permanently.

World.title: Nigeria, Russia Strengthen Customs Cooperation  to Optimise Trade Facilitation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Eromosele Abiodun

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and the Federal Customs Service of the Russian Federation have taken a significant step toward strengthening bilateral customs cooperation after signing an Agreement on Cooperation and Mutual Assistance in Customs Matters (CMAA) in Moscow.

The agreement establishes a framework for closer collaboration in trade facilitation, information exchange, customs enforcement, financial integrity and capacity development, while opening new opportunities for the two administrations to deepen operational cooperation.

The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, who led the Nigerian delegation, described the agreement as a strategic instrument to safeguard economic integrity, secure supply chains and strengthen trade governance. He said the engagement marked the culmination of months of technical consultations, legal reviews, and constructive discussions between both administrations, reflecting a shared commitment to modernising customs operations and responding more effectively to emerging challenges in international trade.

Adeniyi explained that the new legislative framework has accelerated the Service’s transformation, particularly through the adoption of digital systems that have significantly automated customs processes.

According to him, declarations, payments and the submission of supporting documents are increasingly conducted electronically, enabling the Service to improve operational efficiency while facilitating legitimate trade.

He emphasised that revenue generation and trade facilitation are not competing objectives, noting that the NCS approach aligns with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards.

On implementing the agreement, Adeniyi identified exchanging experience between the two countries’ Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) programmes as an important area of cooperation.

He explained that both administrations had been encouraged to undertake structured exchanges to understand their respective programme frameworks, operational procedures and implementation experiences, with the longer-term objective of advancing mutual recognition and acceptance. “Such an arrangement, when developed, would strengthen the confidence accorded to compliant traders and potentially improve the efficiency of cargo movement between the two countries,” he stated.

During bilateral discussions with the Head of the Federal Customs Service of Russia, Mr Valery Pikalyov, Adeniyi highlighted the similarities in the reform journeys of both administrations, explaining that the Service had evolved considerably from its colonial origins into a modern customs administration.

He recalled that the Service’s law remained largely unchanged for several years, until the introduction of the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023, which provided a stronger legal foundation for institutional reforms, technological advancement and private-sector partnerships.

The discussions also examined the prospect of sharing customs statistics and trade data for analytical purposes.

Adeniyi highlighted Nigeria’s participation in the World Customs Organisation’s data initiative, stating that the NCS was the only customs administration to submit its trade data to the WCO data project.

He noted that access to reliable customs data and structured information exchange would support comparative analysis, improve understanding of bilateral trade patterns and strengthen evidence-based customs administration.

In his response, Pikalyov explained that the Federal Customs Service of Russia is statutorily authorised to collect, process, compile and provide customs statistics derived from customs declarations.

He noted that Russia already exchanges customs statistics with foreign customs administrations under existing agreements, allowing both sides to analyse trade flows, identify discrepancies and monitor developments in bilateral commerce.

He indicated that the Russian side was prepared to explore a dedicated arrangement with the NCS to exchange statistical data, subject to the relevant framework and procedures.

World.title: Stock Market Declines Marginally as Investors’ Profit-taking Persist
World.content:
