Kayode Tokede

The domestic stock market extended its negative performance yesterday , as sustained selling pressure dragged the major market indicator lower by 0.02 per cent.

The Nigerian Exchange Limited All-Share Index (NGX ASI) declined by 43.09 basis points, or 0.02 per cent to close at 248,286.56 basis points. Consequently, market capitalisation decreased by N28 billion to close at N161.21 trillion.

Sectoral performance was mixed, as the Insurance (+1.7per cent) and Industrial Goods (+0.1per cent) indices advanced, while the Consumer Goods (-0.3per cent) and Oil & Gas (-0.1per cent) indices declined. Meanwhile the Banking index closed flat.

Analysts noted that “the session was characterised by bearish sentiment and subdued trading activity, as the market recorded another decline alongside contractions in trading volume, transaction value and deal count.”

Market sentiment remained negative, with 26 decliners, outnumbering 19 advancers. Sovereign Trust Insurance led the gainers’ chart, rising 9.96 per cent to close at N2.76, per share. Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC) followed with a gain of 9.94 per cent to close at N3.87, while Chellarams rose 9.86 per cent to close at N11.70, per share.

Cornerstone Insurance advanced by 9.64 per cent to close at N4.55, while Regency Alliance Insurance gained 8.45 per cent to close at 77 kobo, per share.

On the losers’ side, Royal Exchange led the decline, falling by 6.00 per cent to close at 94 kobo, per share. McNichols followed with a decline of 5.05 per cent to close at N4.70, while International Breweries depreciated by 4.50 per cent to close at N9.55, per share.

Veritas Kapital Assurance shed 4.42 per cent to close at N1.08, while Oando lost 4.17 per cent to close at N34.50, per share.

Also, the total volume of trade declined by 17.54 per cent to 372.030 million units, valued at N14.367 billion, and exchanged in 28,467 deals. Transactions in the shares of Trans-Nationwide Express led the activity with 30.251 million shares worth N74.121 million. Chams Holdings Company followed with account of 29.989 million shares valued at N90.908 million, while Fidelity Bank traded 20.097 million shares valued at N460.634 million.

Guaranty Trust Holding Company (GTCO) traded 18.037 million shares worth N2.093 billion, while Sovereign Trust Insurance traded 17.715 million shares worth N47.692 million.

Looking ahead, Cowry Assets Management Limited said, “weak market breadth, subdued trading activity, and lingering sell-side pressure may constrain near-term recovery, although selective bargain-hunting in fundamentally sound counters could provide some support.

“Investors are advised to monitor market trends closely and seek professional advice before making investment decisions.”

World.title: Lush Hair Steals The Spotlight At Lagos Fashion Week 2026
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Lagos Fashion Week 2026 had many unforgettable moments, but one brand turned hair into the loudest fashion statement of the week. As Official Hair Sponsor, Lush Hair transformed its runway into a vibrant celebration of confidence, individuality, and diversity, where every model, every style, and every strand told a story of self-expression. Writes MARY NNAH

Lush Hair did not just show up at Lagos Fashion Week 2026, it owned it, turning the runway into a loud, joyful celebration of what it means to Be Beautiful.

As the Official Hair Sponsor of Lagos Fashion Week 2026, Lush Hair went far beyond showcasing beautiful hairstyles to prove that hair is a powerful expression of identity and personal confidence, bringing fashion, beauty, entertainment and culture together in one vibrant presentation that celebrated confidence, individuality, diversity and self-expression.

Built around its brand philosophy of “Be Beautiful,” Lush Hair went beyond showcasing beautiful hairstyles to show how hair can powerfully express identity and personal confidence.

“For us, ‘Be Beautiful’ is not just a slogan, it is a commitment. We wanted the runway to reflect real women, real stories and real confidence. Every look was about giving every woman permission to own her beauty, in her own way”, said Marketing Manager, Lush Hair (Dry), Vivian Obiano.

It was a celebration of beauty in its many forms, with a diverse cast of models, brand ambassadors, popular personalities, and a special musical performance reinforcing the message that confidence has no single look, age, size or definition.

At the heart of the presentation were three categories, three expressions that brought Lush Hair’s full portfolio to life.

The Lush Hair Extensions category, positioned as Be Confident, celebrated everyday confidence, individuality and the freedom to express oneself through different hairstyles, with brand ambassadors Rachael Okonkwo and Anita Asuoha (Real Warri Pikin) representing the category and showcasing the versatility of Lush Hair’s extension offerings and the confidence they inspire.

The Hair Care category, positioned as Live the Soft Life, was represented by a two-time Guinness World Record winner and Lush Hair care brand ambassador, Hilda Baci which highlighted the importance of healthy hair care as the foundation of beautiful styling with Lush Hair’s hair care products playing an essential role throughout the styling process, from hair preparation and styling to finishing and maintenance, while the showcase also provided an opportunity to introduce Lush Hair Mousse and oil sheen, both upcoming addition to the brand’s hair care portfolio, which will soon be available through its e-commerce platform, open markets and supermarkets.

The LushNova category, Lush Hair’s premium hair extensions range, brought an elevated expression of glamour, sophistication and confidence to the runway, embodying its signature positioning, “You’re That Girl.”, represented by brand ambassador Folasade Adeleke, showcasing the premium side of the Lush Hair portfolio and celebrating women who embrace their individuality and confidently own their presence.

Together, these three categories demonstrated the breadth of Lush Hair’s offerings, from accessible hair extensions and everyday hair care to premium options.

Inclusivity remained at the heart of Lush Hair’s runway storytelling, and the brand deliberately featured a diverse cast of models, including a plus-size model, a model with albinism, a model with tribal marks, and twin models, alongside other distinctive personalities. In a particularly memorable moment, twin child models also graced the runway, reinforcing the message that confidence is not restricted by age.

Through this representation, Lush Hair challenged conventional beauty standards and celebrated the uniqueness of every individual, and rather than presenting one idea of beauty, the runway became a platform for different people to confidently embrace what makes them distinct.

The message was simple: Beauty is diverse, confidence is personal, and everyone deserves to feel seen.

“We deliberately cast for diversity because beauty has never had one face. From our plus-size model to our model with albinism, our model with tribal marks, and our twin models, we wanted every woman watching to see herself on that runway and feel seen”, Vivian added.

Beyond its brand ambassadors, Lush Hair brought together a mix of popular personalities and former Big Brother Naija housemates, adding cultural relevance, excitement and entertainment to the runway, with a lineup that included Temi Nkem, the season 11 Big Brother Naija winner, Godessa, Barry and Chimso Chuka.

The inclusion of male personalities also reinforced the brand’s inclusive approach, demonstrating that confidence and self-expression are not limited by gender, and each personality brought a distinct energy to the runway, creating a presentation that connected beauty, fashion and popular culture.

To complement the hairstyles and bring the runway vision to life, Lush Hair collaborated with fashion designer Desiree Iyama, who created the outfits worn by the models. The partnership brought together fashion design and hairstyling as complementary forms of creative expression, ensuring that the clothing and hair worked together to communicate the confidence and individuality at the centre of the presentation, and the result was a cohesive runway experience where hair was not simply an accessory to fashion but an essential part of each model’s overall look and identity.

Lush Hair concluded its runway presentation with a memorable appearance by Teni the Entertainer, delivering an exciting fusion of music, fashion and beauty. In a standout moment, Teni not only performed for the audience but also modelled Lush Hair extensions, becoming part of the runway experience herself, and her appearance brought an energetic and entertaining close to the showcase, further reinforcing the brand’s celebration of personality, individuality and unapologetic confidence.

One of the most significant aspects of Lush Hair’s participation was its contribution to the wider Lagos Fashion Week experience, because as the Official Hair Sponsor, Lush Hair was responsible for the hairstyling across the fashion week, extending beyond its own runway presentation to the models showcasing collections for other participating designers, including selected offsite shows.

These hairstyles were created by the talented hairstylists and alumni of the Lush Hair Professional School, highlighting the technical expertise, creativity and professional training developed through the brand’s hairstyling education platform.

From hair preparation and installation to styling and finishing, the team worked to bring the designers’ creative visions to life while demonstrating the versatility of Lush Hair’s extension and hair care products. This contribution reinforced Lush Hair’s position not only as a beauty brand but also as an enabler of professional talent, creative excellence and growth within Nigeria’s beauty and fashion industries.

“Beyond the runway, our responsibility was to the whole of Lagos Fashion Week. Our Professional School hair stylists and alumni worked across designers and offsite shows to bring different creative visions to life. That is what Lush Hair stands for, not just products, but people, talent and the growth of the industry”, Vivian added,

In the end, Lush Hair’s participation at Lagos Fashion Week 2026 was ultimately a celebration of confidence in all its forms. Through its three product categories, diverse runway cast, influential brand ambassadors, celebrity appearances, fashion collaboration and memorable musical finale, the brand demonstrated that beauty is not confined to conventional standards. Beyond its own runway showcase, Lush Hair’s role in creating hairstyles across Lagos Fashion Week highlighted its contribution to the wider fashion ecosystem and its commitment to developing professional hairstyling talent.

The overarching message was that confidence belongs to everyone, regardless of appearance, age, body type, or gender, and that hair is one of the many powerful ways people express who they are, and that Lagos Fashion Week 2026 provided Lush Hair with a platform to celebrate this belief while showcasing the creativity, versatility, and expertise behind its products, people, and brand.

“Beautiful hair styling starts with healthy hair. That is why our Hair Care range is the foundation of everything we do. With Live the Soft Life, we are reminding women that caring for your hair is caring for yourself, and our new Lush Hair Mousse and oil sheen are other steps in making that care easy, accessible and enjoyable”, said Senior Brand Manager, Hair Care Category, Lush Hair, Damilola Agboola.

“At the end of the day, confidence belongs to everyone. Whether it is through our extensions, our premium LushNova range, or our Hair Care products, we want every woman to feel that she can Live the Soft Life and Be Beautiful on her own terms”, Agboola added.

World.title: United Nigeria Airlines’ Corporate Philanthropy
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chinedu Eze

Nigeria’s rising carrier, United Nigeria Airlines (UNA) has found a unique way of etching itself in the memories of many individuals.

The airline sponsored football tournament, the Ndigboamaka Traders Cup, a three-week league game that culminated in a novelty match last Saturday with the Nigerian Customs Service football team.

A fortnight ago, United Nigeria Airlines and the Nigerian Cancer Society (NCS) launched the ‘United Against Cancer’ initiative to help create awareness for the early detection and treatment of cancer.

The airline will garner financial support for cancer screening and treatment of cancer patients.

United Nigeria Airlines has shown that a company does not need to operate for 10 years before it begins to support the society, making financial and other commitments to support the community.

In the five years of its existence, United Nigeria Airlines has imbibed the philosophy that stronger brand reputation and customer loyalty is built through philanthropic engagements.

The airline believes that companies that actively support local communities and operate ethically earn public trust and positive publicity. Consumers increasingly favor socially responsible brands, leading to higher customer retention.

So, on Saturday at the National stadium, Surulere, Lagos, the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) football team beat the Ndigboamaka All Stars 1-0 in the novelty match that spiced the grand finale of the United Nigeria Airlines Ndigboamaka Traders Cup.

Speaking on the reason for supporting the football tournament, the Managing Director of United Nigeria Airlines, Chief Osita Okonkwo, said this was the second year the airline has supported the tournament which brings together young men from the association’s 54 member markets across Lagos State.

Okonkwo said the major reason for the sponsorship is UNA’s mission to unite people across the country and continent and the tournament fits that goal. He said the second reason was that sports deliver social, economic and health benefits.

He also said United Nigeria existed to fly people, and that its sponsorship was meant to show members the practical benefits of air travel and encourage them to fly more often.

Okonkwo revealed that as a way of helping Small, Medium Enterprises

(SMEs) to thrive, United Nigeria Airlines offered a special travel package for association members. The package is designed to help traders move their goods more easily.

Okonkwo stated that the long-term aim of building capacity as an airline was for every part of the country to be connected to every other, so that traders and businesses would not be confined to a part of the country, noting that the country is large and rich enough that Nigerians should not have to look elsewhere for opportunities, and remarked that connecting regions would help unite businesses, cultures and people.

He said United Nigeria Airlines loved to partner with groups whose members share its commitment to growth and cross-regional connection.

While speaking, the President of Ndigboamaka Traders Association, Chinedu Ukatu, described the tournament as a unity competition. He said its aim was to bring traders together beyond the market, so that they compete on the pitch rather than quarrel.

Ukatu said the first edition was sponsored by United Nigeria Airlines. He said the tournament will continue regardless of changes in its leadership, because the association itself is meant to outlast its members. He also said organisers want to take the competition beyond Lagos to traders in other states, and eventually to a larger “5.0” edition.

Ukatu said players would receive cash prizes and the association also plans to recommend standout players for sponsorship by football clubs, since trading may not be their long-term career.

The tournament started with the third-place match between Computer Village FC Vs Cooling Parts Dealers Association (COPDAS FC). The match was decided by a penalty shootout, which COPDAS won after a 1-1 draw.

The second match was the novelty match between the Ndigboamaka All Stars and the Nigeria Customs Service football team which ended 1-0 in favour of the NCS.

Reacting to the tournament, the Controller General of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Adewale Adeniyi, who was represented by the Deputy Controller (Admin) Federal Operations Unit Zone A, Timothy Worusen, said the NCS existed to facilitate legitimate trade and that traders can visit any customs command for guidance on what they may or may not bring in. He added that the service worked closely with other agencies, handing over seized arms and amunitions to the police, drugs to the relevant authorities, and food-related cases to a regulatory agency.

He also celebrated the customs team’s novelty-match win and said the service wanted a closer relationship with traders.

The tournament was graced by prominent Nigerians, including the governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State for the 2027 election, Funso Doherty, who said that the tournament reminded him of the old Lagos State where people come from different parts of the country to Lagos and feel at home without harassment and intimidation.

He said: “Lagos has always been a city that is welcoming. It has always been a city that has had people from all over. It’s not something of today. It goes back centuries. We, as indigenous Lagosians, we have welcomed people from everywhere. We have lived peaceably with one another. We understand that everybody brings some measure of value to the society. And it’s in peaceful interaction with one another that we can get the benefit of our respective strengths.”

Doherty, who described the tournament as a community building event, said: “It’s an event where, as a community, we come together to interact with one another. In a business community, it’s not just about the day-to-day business, it’s also about the relationships we build, the way we engage with one another within the society. And this is just an example of that. Like I said, we are supportive of it and continue to identify with it.”

Speaking about the cancer support initiative with Nigeria Cancer Society, United Nigeria Airlines said the first level of the campaign would focus on early-stage prevention, a large-scale awareness drive and the sharing of information; while the second level would address cancers that were not detected early and needed treatment.

“We have heard the news, and we have seen people who have been affected by this deadly disease. It is on that basis that United Nigeria has decided to work with the Nigerian Cancer Society in a special way to mount a campaign against cancer in Nigeria. We have looked at the programmes and activities of the Society, and we are very happy with them. We believe they need to be supported, not only by United Nigeria Airlines through the United Nigeria Airlines Foundation but also by the passengers who fly with us and book tickets on our platform,” Okonkwo said.

World.title: United Nigeria Airlines Launches Jos Flights to Other Cities

United Nigeria Airlines will begin scheduled flight operations linking Jos, the Plateau State capital, with Lagos, Kano and Owerri, giving residents of the state three new connections. The operations will start on November 24, and tickets are already available for purchase.

According to the airline the Lagos–Jos–Lagos operations will be the most frequent of the three, with four flights each week on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. The Jos–Kano–Jos route will operate twice a week, on Tuesdays and Fridays, while the Jos–Owerri–Jos route will also run twice weekly, on Wednesdays and Fridays.

Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership formed part of the state’s broader effort to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunity. He thanked the airline’s management for their confidence in the state’s vision.

The commissioner said the Jos–Owerri route would make it easier for residents of Plateau and neighbouring states to reach the South-East and South-South, supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchange in those regions.

Responding on behalf of United Nigeria Airlines, Managing Director, Chief Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement stood out because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central zones. He described Plateau as a special and strategic state and said the airline intends to meet the standard of service for which it is known.

Ibom Airlines Limited has reported a profit of N5.485 billion for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, sustaining its profitability despite a challenging aviation operating environment.

The results were presented at the airline’s Annual General Meeting (AGM), held on 17 November 2026 at the Victor Attah International Airport, Uyo.

Presenting the audited financial results, the Chairman, Mr. Mfon Udom, said the airline delivered record passenger numbers, record number of flights, and record revenue in 2025, with revenue growing by 52 per cent from N96.53 billion in 2024 to N147.03 billion in 2025. He attributed the sustained profitability to the company’s operational discipline, prudent financial management, and commitment to safety and excellent customer service.

He also emphasised the need for the Shareholder to invest further equity in the airline in 2026 to help shore up its balance sheet and position the airline for the next phase of its growth.

Representing the shareholder, Senator Effiong Bob commended the board, management, and workforce for their dedication to operational excellence and service.

In a statement, the Group Manager, Marketing & Communications for Ibom Air, Aniekan Essienette, said the AGM concluded with a renewed commitment to Ibom Air’s vision of becoming a world-class African regional airline, supported by financial sustainability, service innovation, and operational excellence.

World.title: Rachel Kolisi: ‘Met the love of my life’
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi is in London to promote her Falling Forward project. Images via IG

Rachel Kolisi has set tongues wagging with a social media post about meeting he “love of my life”. The former Springbok WAG and ex-wife of Siya Kolisi is currently in London to promote her book, Falling Forward.

In 2024, Rachel and Siya shared news of their shock marriage split.

Since then, the rugby player has been linked to 25-year-old influencer Rachel John



RACHEL KOLISI SPARKS RUMOURS WITH LATEST POST

On her social media platforms, Rachel Kolisi posted a picture of her enjoying a night out in London.

“Met the love of my life on the underground yesterday”, she captioned the post.

Rachel’s mention of finding love again set tongues wagging in the comments section.

Dozens of followers were convinced Rachel had moved on from her e-husband, Siya Kolisi…

“Only the right person can give you this glow. Love it for you”

“Lucky guy!”



Others were convinced that Rachel was referring to something and not someone…

“She fetched her printed books, which are literally a physical reminder of who she is underneath it all…..she’s reminding herself she is her own love of her life”

“She met herself. She found Rachel”.

Rachel Kolisi is currently in London as part of her international Falling Forward project.

She is booked for a book signing and to host a screening of her personal documentary, followed by a live Q&A session about resilience, faith, motherhood, and rebuilding her life after her high-profile divorce.

NO PLANS TO MOVE ON, YET

Rachel Kolisi has revealed that she has no plans to find love again just yet.

Speaking in an interview on 947 in March, the mom of two said: “I find it so interesting that that’s what’s considered moving on. I’m good by myself. I don’t think I’ve ever been better by myself.”

Rachel has also repeatedly shared that she would not be dropping her last name.

Speaking at a recent book event, Rachel Kolisi responded to a question about why she chose to keep her marital surname, despite her divorce.

She mentioned a time when she was approached by a woman in a supermarket who called her “Siya Kolis’s wife”.

She said of the encounter: “‘I was like ‘Nope’. Then I stopped and said ‘My name is Rachel, it’s nice to meet you’”.

Rachel reflected on why she did not revert to her maiden name, which is Smith.

She continued: “What is really important for me is to create stability for my children in two years, after they have moved five times, three times in schools and twice overseas. It was the most unstable, insane years of their lives, plus their parents got divorced on top of that.

“Stability not just for my children, but for myself and for the people around me. Was a surname change desperately needed at the time? No. Will I do it eventually? I don’t know. Why is the public so intrigued about this? I have no idea. But for now, I’m Rachel Kolisi, and I’m very proud to be Rachel Kolisi”.

World.title: Love Is Blind SA’s ‘messy’ male cast make international headlines
World.content:
Love Is Blind SA's male cast have made headlines around the world, weeks before its premiere. Images via IG

The male cast of Love Is Blind South Africa have made headlines abroad after Netflix posted, and then deleted, their images – twice!

Interestingly, the men’s job titles also changed overnight.

The dating reality TV show is hosted by married couple Dineo Langa and Solo Langa, and will premiere with its first 6 episodes on Friday, 4 November.



The show brings together 27 singles – 14 women and 13 men – aged between 24 and 3, who will find love behind a wall.

LOVE IS BLIND SOUTH AFRICA’S MALE CAST MAKE INTERNATIONAL HEADLINES

On social media, Netflix’s decision to post and delete images of the male cast members on Love Is Blind SA’s debut season has become a trending topic.

Many South Africans commented on the supposed disparity in appearances and career choices between the men and women cast members.

Others dug up the dirt on a few individuals.

US reality TV podcaster, Rikki Wise, of Storytime with Rikki, picked up on Netflix’s faux pas, adding: “It’s crazy that they changed all these people’s photos and job titles and thought we wouldn’t notice…I cannot believe they did this”.

Rikki expressed her concern that “None of these men has real jobs… it just means unemployed!”



She added: “The women are scientists and attorneys and doctors, and this is what you gave them? This is a sh*tshow. Get it together!”

Fellow US podcaster, Jessie Woo, commented under a Love Is Blind SA post: “Why did y’all delete this the first time?”.

UK reality TV podcaster, Anthony Gilet, agreed, adding that Netflix was “messy” over the move.

Referring to rumours about the cast’s questioning paths, he added in an IG post: “We’re talking secret baby mamas, drowning in debt, down-low estcourt trade!”

WHEN DOES FIRST SEASON PREMIERE?

Love Is Blind SA, which follows the US franchise, will air its first six episodes on Friday, 4 December.

Episodes 7 and 8 will air on 11 December, with the grand finale taking place on 18 December.

South Africa has adapted several popular international TV dating shows for local audiences. These also include Netflix’s The Ultimatum: South Africa, and Love Never Lies: South Africa. Other local adaptations include Love Island South Africa and Married at First Sight: Mzansi.

World.title: ‘Weddings and funerals to eat’: Pensioner’s grim survival plan has South Africans talking
World.content:
Older South Africans who depend on their SASSA pension say the money no longer covers the month, and one commenter has a bleak suggestion for getting by.

The comments appeared under a post on The South African’s Facebook page, where pensioners and their families discussed how they survive on the grant.

Surviving on a pension FOR PENSIONERS

Daniel Lebatie addressed his fellow pensioners directly, and offered a plan that mixed humour with hardship.



“Hi senior citizen of SA, to survive on your monthly pension, we should go to parties, weddings, and funerals to eat at weekends; maybe just maybe we’ll survive with the little money we get,” Lebatie wrote.

His comment drew laughing and heart reactions, but it touched on a real worry for many households where the old age grant is the main income.

A shortfall that hits home

One commenter shared The South African’s earlier report on a grant shortfall. In that story, a pensioner’s money dropped from R1 300 to R633.

Stories like that one strike a nerve because many older grant recipients do not spend their pension on themselves alone. They often spend it on grandchildren, unemployed adult children and other relatives who share the same roof.

Palesa Rose Motsôane said older recipients also face judgement over how they spend the grant. “Even the elderly buy alcohol with their grants, even gambling with it. Am I wrong, or just because they are older that we are not to say anything?” she wrote.

‘Half for ministers’

Some commenters directed their anger at government rather than at recipients.



Others echoed calls made in SASSA comment threads for the government to create jobs so that grandparents do not have to support whole families on a single grant.

For now, many pensioners say they have no option but to stretch every rand until payday.

World.title: Durban security boss Ferrel Govender dies in custody
World.content:
Correctional Services has launched an investigation into the death of murder-accused Durban businessman Ferrel Govender. Image: X

Murder-accused Durban businessman and former Pro Secure CEO Ferrel Govender has died in custody at the age of 41.

The Department of Correctional Services (DCS) confirmed his death on Wednesday, 18 November.

Govender faced charges of premeditated murder following the fatal shooting of Umhlanga businessman Shailen Singh in December 2024.



FERREL GOVENDER’S DEATH UNDER INVESTIGATION

Correctional Services spokesperson Singabakho Nxumalo confirmed that authorities admitted Govender to the Durban Correctional Facility on 15 January 2025.

“At the time of his death, he was awaiting his next court appearance, which had been scheduled for 27 May 2027,” Nxumalo said.

“In line with established procedures governing cases of unnatural death within correctional facilities, an investigation will be conducted to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.”

Nxumalo said the department would engage with Govender’s family and provide further details while respecting their privacy.

Govender reportedly died in hospital.

The department has yet to confirm his cause of death.



THE MURDER OF SHAILEN SINGH

Police arrested Govender and his younger brother, Darren, in January 2025 in connection with Singh’s murder.

Gunmen opened fire on the 32-year-old businessman as he sat in his vehicle in a parking lot on Meridian Drive in Umhlanga on 29 December 2024.

Singh died at the scene.

The State alleged that an affair between Singh and Ferrel Govender’s girlfriend motivated the killing.

Prosecutors also claimed that CCTV footage placed both brothers at the crime scene.

Both brothers denied the allegations.

FIVE FAILED BIDS FOR BAIL

While Darren secured R200 000 bail in February 2025, Ferrel fought unsuccessfully for his release.

He approached several courts, including the Supreme Court of Appeal, in his bid to secure bail.

His murder trial began in the Durban High Court in July 2026.

Govender died before the State could conclude its case against him.

GOVENDER FAMILY WANTS ANSWERS

Govender’s attorney, Avir Maharaj, told The Mercury that the family would request an inquest into his death.

Meanwhile, National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) spokesperson Natasha Ramkisson-Kara said prosecutors were awaiting formal documentation.

“A death certificate for court purposes has to be produced,” she said.

Darren Govender remains out on bail and still faces prosecution in connection with Singh’s murder.

World.title: Geordin Hill-Lewis vows to deliver for Cape Town
World.content:
Cape Town mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis outlined his administration’s priorities for the next five years during his inaugural address. Image: City of Cape Town

Democratic Alliance (DA) leader Geordin Hill-Lewis has been sworn in for a second term as Cape Town mayor, a day after dismissing reports of a proposed mayoral swap with Helen Zille.

Hill-Lewis took office on Thursday, 19 November, during the inaugural council meeting at the Cape Town Civic Centre.

Xanthea Limberg was elected deputy mayor, while Felicity Purchase retained her position as Speaker.



HILL-LEWIS BACK FOR ANOTHER FIVE YEARS

The DA retained its outright majority in Cape Town following the 2026 local government elections.

Cape Town is the only metro in South Africa where a single political party secured an outright majority.

In his inaugural address, Hill-Lewis described serving as mayor as the “best job in the world”.



“I am humbled and blessed by this extraordinary opportunity. And I intend to make every single day count,” he said.

FIVE PROMISES TO CAPE TOWN RESIDENTS

Hill-Lewis outlined five priorities for his second term:

Stronger policing: Establishing a municipal detective unit and investing in crime-fighting technology.

Establishing a municipal detective unit and investing in crime-fighting technology. More jobs: Attracting investment and growing employment opportunities.

Attracting investment and growing employment opportunities. Reliable and affordable services: Improving municipal infrastructure and reducing sewage spills.

Improving municipal infrastructure and reducing sewage spills. Affordable housing: Releasing more city-owned land for housing and upgrading informal settlements.

Releasing more city-owned land for housing and upgrading informal settlements. A cleaner city: Tackling illegal dumping and improving the cleanliness of neighbourhoods and public spaces.

Hill-Lewis also vowed to continue fighting for greater investigative powers for municipal police officers.



WHAT ABOUT THE MAYORAL SWAP?

Hill-Lewis’s inauguration follows speculation that he could head to Johannesburg, paving the way for Zille’s return to the Mother City.

The DA leader confirmed that several people had approached him with the idea but denied formally proposing the swap to ActionSA.

Meanwhile, Zille has shrugged off suggestions of a return to Cape Town.



The DA faces an uphill battle to secure control of Johannesburg amid ongoing coalition negotiations.

World.title: SA Explained | South Africa Has Voted. But Who Will Govern Your Metro? | 19 November 2026
World.content:
The Ballot Decides The Seats. The Negotiating Table Decides The Government.

South Africa's local elections have exposed a difficult democratic question: how should political parties turn fragmented results into legitimate, accountable municipal governments?

South Africans can spend months debating which party deserves to win an election, only to discover that the more consequential contest begins after the ballots have been counted. A party can secure the largest share of support in a municipality and still find itself unable to govern. Another can finish some distance behind, yet acquire considerable influence over who becomes mayor.

That is the paradox of coalition politics. Elections establish the distribution of political power, but negotiations determine how that power is exercised. For residents waiting for functioning infrastructure, reliable services and accountable leadership, the distinction is anything but academic.

When winning is not enough

The aftermath of the 2026 local government elections has brought this reality into focus. The ANC's declining support, the DA's electoral position and ActionSA's growing significance in coalition negotiations have created a political environment in which no single party can necessarily dictate the outcome.

Johannesburg illustrates the difficulty. The challenge is not simply identifying the largest party, but establishing which combination of parties can command sufficient council support to elect a mayor, pass budgets and sustain the administration.

Every additional coalition partner potentially introduces another set of priorities, demands and disagreements. A governing majority assembled from several parties may be mathematically possible without being politically durable.

This is where election analysis often stops too early. Coalition arithmetic establishes who can govern together. It does not establish whether they can govern effectively.

The difference between a coalition and a government

A coalition agreement is ultimately a framework for sharing political responsibility. It must provide answers to questions that extend far beyond who receives the mayoral chain or which party controls a particular portfolio.

What happens when coalition partners disagree over a budget? Who carries responsibility when service-delivery targets are missed? How will disputes be resolved without repeatedly threatening the administration's survival?

These questions become particularly important in municipalities where voters have already experienced political instability. An agreement that settles the immediate leadership contest but leaves operational responsibilities unclear risks transferring uncertainty from the negotiating table into council chambers.

The most consequential test of a coalition is therefore not whether it survives its first mayoral vote. It is whether it can make difficult decisions consistently enough for the municipality to function.

Do voters still have a say after election day?

Coalition negotiations create another tension: parties may enter agreements with political opponents they campaigned against. Such arrangements can be legitimate within the electoral system, but their legitimacy should not depend solely on whether they meet the legal requirements for forming a majority.

Voters are entitled to understand why a partnership was chosen, what compromises were made and which commitments remain in force.

That is why transparency matters. Publishing the principles and commitments underpinning a coalition would give residents a clearer basis for judging the administration. It would also make it harder for political leaders to shift responsibility when agreements begin to unravel.

Accountability becomes especially difficult when every coalition partner can claim credit for success while blaming someone else for failure.

The real verdict comes after the deal

The results of a local election can reveal public frustration, changing party loyalties and the emergence of new political forces. But those signals are only the beginning of the democratic process.

The decisions made after the election will determine whether political parties treat the result as an opportunity to build workable institutions or simply as another contest over office.

A coalition's true measure will not be the number of signatures on its founding agreement. It will be the quality of its decisions, the clarity of its accountability and the services that residents experience.

South Africans have already decided how their councils should be composed. The next question is whether the politicians negotiating in their name can turn those results into governments that work.

World.title: UAE candidate says her 'bridge builder' skills make her the woman to lead UN
World.content:
NEW YORK - Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati candidate vying to become the next UN secretary general, told AFP she believes she is a "bridge builder" who can effect a positive change at a crucial time for the organisation.

An Emirati with Palestinian roots, Nusseibeh emerged recently as a candidate following an impasse in the race.

Ahead of a new vote at the UN Security Council to choose a successor to Antonio Guterres, the diplomat said: "It's not easy to be an Arab woman campaigning...

"But I'm not campaigning because I'm an Arab woman. I'm campaigning because I believe in the UN."

If elected, she would be the first woman to lead the global body and the second Arab after Egyptian Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

She stepped down from her post as state minister at the UAE foreign ministry and as envoy to the UN and EU to campaign for the UN job.

A seasoned diplomat, she has also served as the UAE's permanent representative to the UN, from 2013 to 2024, the first woman to hold the post.

Her family has traditionally held the role of opening and closing the door to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in the walled Old City of Jerusalem, after the Christian community entrusted the responsibility to this Muslim family.

"My family has it in its DNA that religion and ethnicity and national identity should never be a divider but a force for coming together for convergence," she told AFP.

She says she "has the ability to bridge differences in perspectives on really difficult issues".

"I believe I have dedicated over a decade to demonstrating what being a bridge builder can do in my diplomacy on the most complex files."

She has consistently defended the UAE's decision to normalise ties with Israel in 2020.

– 'Generational change' –

She cites as an example a visit she organised in November 2023, after the Hamas attack against Israel on October 7 that sparked the Gaza war.

She took Security Council ambassadors to the Rafah crossing point between Egypt and Gaza, where they saw warehouses filled with maternity kits, medical supplies and wheelchairs that were not entering the Palestinian territory.

"When ambassadors saw that, it brought to life for them that what we are doing in New York is not debating diplomatic texts. We are trying to prevent suffering on the ground for the people who need it the most," she said.

The visit helped pass two UN resolutions, one of which created a mechanism to speed up the delivery of aid.

Nusseibeh says the UN is experiencing a moment of "generational change" and must reject the idea of "managed decline".

In her first 100 days in the job, she would identify key conflicts to be addressed quickly by a strengthened leadership team and a mediation council that she plans to create.

Reforming the UN will require "a political mind, but also with decisiveness to take some quick decisions", she said.

- 'Fully independent' -

Rights groups have challenged her candidacy, citing accusations the UAE has supported Sudanese paramilitaries in the country's war with the regular army, allegations Abu Dhabi has denied.

"There is obviously a lot of public debate about any candidacy, but a lot about mine," she said.

"I am independent. I have taken a leave of absence from my government... I would be fully independent."

She added that she held firm in the face of criticism thanks partly to support from 25 women's organisations in Afghan civil society that threw their weight behind her campaign.

She met some of these women during previous negotiations on resolutions concerning Afghanistan, she said.

"Those are the people I would want to serve if I was successful."

Nusseibeh said she is also thinking of the children and women of Gaza and Sudan.

"It's often the women and the children who suffer, the men who decide to go to war."

World.title: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir gets 3-year ban for doping
World.content:
NAIROBI - Reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been banned for three years for doping, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday, in the latest blow to the reputation of Kenyan athletics.

The highly decorated 33-year-old Jepchirchir, who also won Olympic gold in the Covid-delayed Tokyo Games in 2021, was suspended after an out-of-competition sample showed traces of the banned blood booster EPO.

The AIU confirmed she had been given a full ban for three years from October 20.

Two other Kenyan runners were banned.

Veronica Loleo, half-marathon silver medallist at the World Road Running Championships in 2026, was given three years for the same offence.

And Ronald Korir, a fourth-place finisher in the 2023 Berlin Marathon, received a six-year ban after he was unable to explain abnormalities in his Athlete Biological Passport.

They join more than 140 Kenyan athletes, including current women's marathon world record-holder Ruth Chepngetich, who have been suspended or banned by the AIU since 2017.

"The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go," AIU chief executive Brett Clothier said in a statement.

The AIU said Jepchirchir's out-of-competition sample had been collected in Kenya prior to her victory in the Sydney Marathon in August.

Jepchirchir has had a lauded career -- a former world record-holder in the half-marathon, a four-time World Marathon Major winner, and titles in the 2024 London Marathon, the 2022 Boston Marathon, and the 2021 New York Marathon.

The decision of World Athletics to award Nairobi the 2029 world championships is likely to increase the scrutiny of the east African nation's anti-doping policies.

"The suspensions are a big blow to our current push to fight doping. It hurts our national integrity and pride as a nation," said Peninah Wahome, head of the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya (ADAK).

"It's an individual decision by an athlete to dope, and let's not condemn all the athletes. Those who have been caught go to show that we're making good progress and we will continue to safeguard clean athletes who are prepared to protect the country's image," she told AFP.

Kenya hosted a three-day visit from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) last month, the body's chief Witold Banka telling the country that it had to strive for zero tolerance on doping.

"Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean," Banka said.

World.title: Climate pressures hit global wine production again: report
World.content:
PARIS - Global wine production is expected to decline again in 2026 as climate change continues to disrupt grape harvests around the world, a report by the International Organisation of Vine and Wine said Wednesday.

"Overall, global wine production reflects climatic pressures on yields alongside a longer-term contraction of vineyard area in several major producing countries", the OIV said in its annual report.

Production and harvesting decisions were also factors, along with "a backdrop of declining global wine consumption and changing patterns of demand", it added.

Wine production is estimated at between 220 and 230 million hectolitres, broadly in line with 2025 levels, the report said.

Using the midpoint estimate of 225 million hectolitres, output would be 7 percent below the average of the past five years.

World wine production fell to its lowest level since 1961 in 2024

In Europe, grape harvests are expected to be 6 percent below their five-year average in 2026 after France and Italy were hit by drought and heatwaves, while Spain and Portugal also struggled.

If the OIV's estimates are confirmed, the last three years would mark the weakest run of wine production this century in Europe, which still accounts for more than 60 percent of global production.

Italy remains the world's leading wine producer, ahead of France and Spain.

Wine production in the US, the world's fourth-largest producer, is running 18 percent below its five-year average.

- Climate impact -

"The most noticeable thing about this year is, as in the previous three years, the impact of climate events", John Barker, OIV's director general, told AFP.

"The general trend therefore appears to be that climate change is creating volatility in production volumes" in both hemispheres, he said.

Production in the southern hemisphere is down 3 percent over five years, with small harvests recorded in top wine-producing countries Australia, Argentina and New Zealand.

This year, South Africa became the leading producer in the southern hemisphere, overtaking Argentina, which was hit by late frosts.

South Africa's growth however was not enough to offset the negative overall performance of the region.

Barker nonetheless pointed to pockets of resilience and recovery, notably in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state, which was hit by historic flooding in 2024.

World.title: Number Of The Day | R17.36c | 19 November 2026
World.content:
The Rand Is Weakening, But That Does Not Tell Us Everything About South Africa's Economy

An exchange rate is often treated as a national economic report card. When the rand strengthens, confidence rises. When it weakens, questions quickly turn to government policy, political instability and the country's economic prospects. Yet a currency's value is not determined by domestic performance alone. Sometimes the explanation lies thousands of kilometres away.

On 19 November 2026, the rand reached R17.36 against the US dollar, its weakest level of the year. The movement came as investors considered the possibility of higher American interest rates, while South Africa faced its own concerns about inflation, commodity prices and political uncertainty.

The temptation is to look at R17.36 and conclude that something has gone wrong in South Africa. The reality is considerably more complicated.

The exchange rate has two sides

When the rand weakens against the dollar, there are at least two questions worth asking. Has the rand become less attractive, or has the dollar become more attractive?

The distinction matters because global investment decisions can affect South Africa even when little has changed domestically. If investors expect American assets to offer stronger returns, they may shift capital towards the United States. That increases demand for dollars while reducing demand for currencies in other markets.

Rand Swiss's Gary Boyson describes the latest movement as more of a dollar story than a rand story. His argument highlights a vulnerability shared by emerging-market economies: domestic currencies are exposed to international financial conditions that their governments cannot control.

South Africa's political uncertainties and economic fundamentals still matter. But an explanation that relies entirely on domestic events risks overlooking the wider movement of global capital.

The Reserve Bank faces an uncomfortable choice

A weaker rand can increase the local cost of imported goods, creating additional pressure on inflation. That presents a challenge for the South African Reserve Bank, whose interest-rate decisions influence borrowing costs, spending and investment.

Higher interest rates can support a currency by making local financial assets more attractive. They can also help control inflation by reducing demand. But these benefits come with economic costs.

Consider a business deciding whether to develop a mine, expand a factory or finance new equipment. The investment must generate enough income to justify the money required. As borrowing costs rise, projects that previously appeared viable can become too expensive to pursue.

This is the difficulty with using interest rates to respond to every economic problem. Monetary tightening can restrain spending, but it cannot directly repair infrastructure, improve public administration or remove structural inefficiencies.

For an economy struggling to generate stronger growth, that distinction is critical. Protecting purchasing power matters, but so does preserving the conditions needed for investment and employment.

Why yesterday's good exchange rate becomes today's bad one

There is another reason to be careful about interpreting currency movements: expectations change.

A few years ago, when the rand traded around R20 against the dollar, an exchange rate of R17.36 might have been welcomed as a substantial improvement. After a period of trading closer to R16, however, the same R17.36 level can feel like a significant setback.

The number has not changed. The reference point has.

This is an example of recency bias, where recent experience shapes what people regard as normal. In financial markets, it can encourage exaggerated reactions to movements that deserve a longer historical comparison.

None of this means a weaker rand is harmless. Exchange-rate movements have real consequences for importers, businesses, consumers and inflation. Nor does historical volatility guarantee that the currency will recover.

It means that understanding the rand requires more than watching the latest number turn red or green. The useful questions concern what is driving the movement, whether those forces are temporary or persistent, and how the effects will reach the wider economy.

An exchange rate can tell us what investors are willing to pay for a currency. It cannot, on its own, tell us everything about the country behind it.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 0 | 19 November 2026
World.content:
Interest Rates Are Standing Still. South Africa's Cost-of-Living Crisis Isn't.

South Africa has avoided another interest rate increase, but the relief many households are waiting for remains elusive. The South African Reserve Bank's decision to leave the repo rate unchanged at 7.25% on 19 November may offer borrowers a measure of stability. It does not, however, reverse the accumulation of financial pressure that has shaped household budgets.

For millions of South Africans, the distinction between economic stability and financial recovery is increasingly important. A pause in interest rate increases can prevent additional pressure, but it cannot automatically restore purchasing power, compensate for lost income or make essential goods cheaper.

The Difference Between Slower Inflation And Lower Prices

October's consumer inflation reading reached 5.2%, up from 4.5% in September and considerably above the Reserve Bank's 3% target. Higher fuel costs have played an important role in pushing inflation upwards, complicating the central bank's efforts to bring price growth under control.

Yet even when inflation moderates, consumers may see little immediate improvement in what they pay. Inflation measures the rate at which prices change. A reduction from 5.2% to 4%, for example, would mean prices are generally increasing more slowly, not that the cost of groceries, transport and other essentials has returned to earlier levels.

This distinction helps explain why improvements in economic indicators can coexist with considerable financial anxiety. Families do not experience inflation as an abstract percentage. They encounter it when calculating how much food their income can purchase, whether they can afford transport to work, and how much remains after meeting existing debt obligations.

Economist Xhanti Payi, speaking to Francis Herd on eNCA's Number of the Day, highlighted the continuing pressure on real disposable income and the additional strain created by unemployment within households. His broader concern points to something easily overlooked in monetary policy discussions: financial resilience depends not only on the cost of borrowing, but also on the number of people earning an income and how far that income stretches.

Why The Reserve Bank Cannot Solve Every Price Problem

Interest rates are a powerful mechanism for managing inflation, but they cannot directly resolve every cause of rising prices. Higher borrowing costs can discourage spending and help contain inflation expectations. They cannot produce more agricultural goods, repair disrupted shipping networks or eliminate international conflicts that increase fuel costs.

That limitation is particularly relevant to South Africa's current inflation outlook. The Reserve Bank has identified continuing geopolitical and fuel-price pressures, while warning that El Niño-related dry conditions could damage harvests and raise food prices.

These risks illustrate the difficult choices confronting monetary policymakers. Raising interest rates too aggressively may increase the burden on indebted households and businesses. Holding rates steady, meanwhile, requires confidence that existing monetary restrictions remain sufficient to prevent inflation from becoming entrenched.

The distinction is especially important when temporary price shocks begin influencing longer-term behaviour. If businesses expect costs to remain elevated, they may adjust their prices accordingly. If workers expect sustained inflation, wage demands can respond. What begins as an external price shock can gradually become a more persistent domestic challenge.

The Missing Ingredient Is Sustainable Income Growth

The financial circumstances of South African households cannot improve substantially through interest rate decisions alone. Greater economic growth, job creation and improvements in disposable income are essential to any sustained recovery in living standards.

This places renewed importance on structural reforms that enable businesses to invest, expand and employ more people. Reliable electricity, efficient logistics, functioning infrastructure and credible public finances matter because they influence the cost and confidence associated with economic activity.

A business considering expansion must assess more than borrowing costs. It needs confidence that electricity will be available, goods can move reliably and economic conditions will support future demand. Improvements in these areas can create opportunities that monetary policy, acting alone, cannot deliver.

There is also an important distinction between improving national economic conditions and ensuring that households benefit from those improvements. Investment must ultimately translate into productive activity, employment and incomes if ordinary South Africans are to experience recovery rather than simply hear about it.

Stability Is A Starting Point, Not The Destination

The Reserve Bank's decision to hold rates creates a degree of predictability in an uncertain economic environment. But stability in borrowing costs is only one component of a much larger economic challenge.

The meaningful test of recovery will not be whether interest rates remain unchanged at the next announcement. It will be whether inflation becomes less persistent, essential expenses become more manageable relative to incomes, and economic growth produces opportunities for households that have spent years absorbing financial pressure.

For South Africans, the real measure of progress is not merely what happens to the repo rate. It is whether the money coming into a household can finally begin to go further.

World.title: Kalonzo and Gachagua storm out of IEBC talks over poll preparedness
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Chief Justice David Maraga confers with DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka after they staged a walkout during a consultative forum with IEBC in Nairobi on November 19, 2026. [ Jenipher Wachie, Standard]

Opposition leaders staged a walkout during a high-level consultative forum with the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), citing exclusion from election preparedness.

The Opposition leaders, led by Kalonzo Musyoka (Wiper), Rigathi Gachagua (Democracy for Citizens Party – DCP), Edwin Sifuna (Linda Mwananchi Movement), Justin Muturi (Democratic Party) and Eugene Wamalwa (DAP-K), accused the IEBC of sidelining them and failing to honour an agreement reached in January this year to form a technical team to discuss and review various electoral concerns.

"During our last engagement with the IEBC on January 28, 2026, and submission of various written communications, we raised pertinent matters touching on the preparedness of the IEBC to conduct the August 2027 General Election. Regrettably, to date, the IEBC has not responded or adhered to the resolutions passed therein," Gachagua told the IEBC commissioners.

Gachagua said the Opposition had resolved to engage the electoral commission through their "People's Coalition on Electoral Reforms", which he said is led by former Chief Justice David Maraga.

The former Deputy President added that the Opposition had tabled mandatory electoral reforms that would facilitate an election of integrity.

"These include monthly engagements with the IEBC to review and discuss milestones towards election preparedness to meet the constitutional tests in Articles 81, 83, 86 and 138 of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. We refuse to allow Kenyans to sleepwalk into a rigged election cycle," he said.

After staging the walkout, Kalonzo said they had honoured the IEBC's invitation in good faith and expected the same in return.

"Good faith is shown in deeds: an independent, impartial and prepared Commission. Today, we did not find it. So we have walked out. Let it be clear: we will not sit in a room and lend our names and faces to the formalisation of a bundled election before the August 2027 General Election. Not today, not ever, and certainly not under our watch," he said.

He added: "Kenyans deserve their voices to be heard and every vote counted at the polling station, verified in the open and declared as cast. Not manufactured. Not padded with the names of people who are not on the voter roll. Kenya deserves nothing less."

Gachagua warned: "The People of Kenya have instructed us that there should be no decision, no discussion that should go on without their involvement. IEBC must know that election is about the people. We have on several occasions requested for engagement and clarification of issues that the people of Kenya wanted addressed ahead of 10th August 2027 polls, but IEBC has remained non-commital and unresponsive. This is mockery of democracy and freedoms that the people of Kenya have fought for."

"Being treated to spin and public trickery by a commission that draws taxpayers money shall be resisted and it is unwarranted. To IEBC, once you decide to listen to the 55 million Kenyans, we shall engage accordingly," he added.

Other demands listed by the Opposition include a comprehensive audit of the voter register, requiring the IEBC to remove duplicate entries, deceased persons and other ineligible names while ensuring all qualified Kenyans are registered.

They also called for an end to the centralised tallying of presidential votes at Bomas of Kenya, arguing that constituency-level declarations should form the basis of the final outcome, with the national tallying centre limited to receiving, compiling and announcing transmitted results.

Additionally, the Opposition wants the IEBC to pilot secure electronic voting for Kenyans in the diaspora and introduce mandatory livestreaming of voting. They also want greater transparency in the procurement of election technology and materials.

However, the Opposition leaders' decision to stage a walkout was heavily criticised by representatives of other political parties, including ODM and the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), which were represented by Kisii Governor Simba Arati, the party's Deputy Party Leader, and Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, respectively.

"It was unfortunate that the Opposition leaders staged a walkout instead of presenting their issues to the IEBC. We know their game. They want to create a perception that they were sidelined so that when they are defeated, they might turn to the courts using that justification. But we are here, and we have witnessed their games," Arati said.

On her part, Mbarire opposed the Opposition's proposal to form a technical committee, maintaining that it was against the law.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon criticised the Opposition leaders, saying the commission was transparent and ready to explain every process. However, he maintained that the commission would not allow itself to be overrun by politicians.

"We have nothing to hide since our mandate is to conduct free and fair elections. We are ready to share the status of our preparedness with political players, who are key stakeholders in the electoral process," he said.

However, the chairperson expressed the commission's concern and disappointment over the multiple court cases it was facing, saying the cases threatened its ability to adhere to strict legal timelines and risked interfering with its mandate to deliver the polls.

He cited challenges in procuring electoral materials, including technology and ballot papers, as well as the recruitment of the commission's Chief Executive Officer (CEO). He accused some Kenyans of putting their selfish interests ahead of patriotism.

"What concerns us is that while we are working hard to meet crucial electoral deadlines, some other Kenyans are working hard to bring us down. For example, the recruitment of a CEO will help us manage the secretariat. We appeal to stakeholders, both state and non-state actors, to be mindful of statutory deadlines that are cast in stone," he said.

He also urged the Judiciary to expedite the cases, saying any further delays would affect the commission's ability to conduct the elections.

Trust deficit among Kenyans compounds the legal hurdles that the commission faces in its quest to conduct free and fair polls.

All the commissioners and the chairperson are new, with critics arguing that they lack the much-needed institutional memory to conduct verifiable polls.

Additionally, the commissioners continue to face the tag of being political godfathers’ protégés, having been appointed following a political rapprochement between the Kenya Kwanza administration and the ODM party. A section of political players claims they could still be answerable to their political masters.

Last week, Ethekon decried a shortage of staff to assist the commission in preparing for the General Election.

He noted that the commission needed to urgently fill key positions, including that of the CEO, among 10 other positions.

Despite advertising seven vacancies – Director of Voter Education and Partnerships, Director of Research, Electoral Boundaries and Risk Management, Director of Human Resources and Administration, Director of Internal Audit and Compliance, Director of Finance, Director of Corporate Communications, and Director of Counties and Constituencies Coordination – the commission had not started conducting interviews a month later.

The IEBC  had indicated that the deadline for applications was August 17.

The acting directors have reportedly been operating in a climate of fear, a situation that has seen the secretariat descend into decision-making paralysis, with officials reluctant to make consequential decisions because their authority and tenure remain uncertain.

“Those serving in an acting capacity have been vulnerable to manipulation, with the hope that they might eventually be confirmed. At the same time, there has been an authority vacuum, as some of them do not feel able to make substantive decisions.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.
