World.title: Oil prices edge higher as Houthi attacks on Riyadh raise supply concerns
World.content:
TOKYO: Oil prices edged ‌higher on Friday, though set for a weekly decline, as concerns over supply disruptions grew following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions ​in the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude futures rose 24 cents, or 0.3 percent, to $92.22 a barrel by 0118 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures for December climbed 19 cents, or 0.2 percent, to $83.40 a barrel, while the more-active January contract gained 20 cents, or 0.2 percent, to $82.64.

Both benchmarks settled little changed on Thursday but Brent is set for a 3.5 percent decline for the week while the December WTI contract is set ‌for a ‌6 percent weekly drop as expectations of a ​supply surplus ‌grew ⁠because ​crude shipments ⁠through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels. Brent and WTI are set to fall for the third week in a row.

“Concerns over Middle Eastern crude oil supplies have resurfaced due to attacks on Riyadh by the Houthis, prompting buying,” said Satoru Yoshida, a commodity analyst with Rakuten Securities.

“Expectations that coordinated production cuts will continue at the ⁠OPEC+ meeting later this month are also providing support,” ‌he said.

The Iran-aligned Houthi movement had been firing missiles toward civilian targets and commercial centers in Saudi Arabia.

Two oil tankers also hit naval mines in the ‌Strait of Hormuz and “exploded” and “are burning,” Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a statement carried by state media on Thursday.

OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their 2027 output policy. The group comprises ‌the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies such as Russia.

The Middle East conflict has caused ⁠the biggest disruption ever ⁠to global oil and gas trade and could cut world oil demand by more than 4 percent by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday.

In Russia, crude oil output could fall again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify, analysts and traders say. Ukrainian drone attacks have slashed Russian oil refineries’ combined crude processing volumes by 45 percent since late October, Reuters reported on Wednesday.

Separately on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin said that Moscow would hit back hard after Ukraine struck ​the bridge linking Russia and Crimea ​for a third time this week and said he was dropping any idea of a moratorium on attacking energy sectors and shipping.

World.title: GCC chief calls for stronger Gulf-Mediterranean security cooperation amid regional threats
World.content:
NAPLES: Iranian attacks on Gulf states and Houthi assaults on Saudi Arabia underscore the need for stronger regional and international cooperation to protect security, maritime navigation and economic stability, Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi said Thursday.

Albudaiwi called for closer strategic ties between Gulf and Mediterranean countries, saying their security interests were increasingly intertwined through energy supplies, trade, investment and vital shipping routes.

His remarks, posted on the GCC Secretariat's website, came at the opening of the Mediterranean Dialogues 2026 forum in Naples, Italy, where he said stability in the Arabian Gulf and Mediterranean was essential to international security.

Albudaiwi thanked Mediterranean countries for standing with GCC states against Iranian attacks and Houthi assaults on Saudi Arabia.



"These stances reflect the depth of the bonds of friendship and cooperation and embody the importance of international solidarity in confronting threats targeting the security, sovereignty, and stability of states," he stressed.

Interconnected maritime chokepoints

He said the Gulf and Mediterranean could no longer be viewed as separate geopolitical regions, given their interconnected interests and exposure to regional crises that can disrupt global energy markets, supply chains and food security.

Developments in the Gulf can affect energy prices in Europe, supply chains across the Mediterranean and food security in Africa, Albudaiwi said, stressing that regional security and economic prosperity had become inseparable.



“Ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Suez Canal is a shared international interest, rather than a matter of limited regional concern,” he pointed out.

He said GCC states continued to pursue de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy, while backing mediation efforts, humanitarian responses and stability in neighboring countries. Any regional security framework, he added, should uphold international law, state sovereignty and non-interference.

Albudaiwi also reiterated the GCC’s position that lasting peace in the region required a just settlement of the Palestinian issue based on a two-state solution, with an independent Palestinian state along the June 4, 1967 borders and East Jerusalem as its capital.

Expanding trade and economic ties

Turning to economic ties, he pointed to growing cooperation between the GCC and Mediterranean countries, including a memorandum of understanding signed in July between the GCC General Secretariat and Italy’s Foreign Ministry covering strategic dialogue and economic cooperation.

A proposed GCC-Med9 ministerial trade meeting in Italy in January is expected to open further avenues for trade, investment and economic integration between Gulf states and the nine Mediterranean EU countries.

Priorities for Gulf-European partnership

Albudaiwi outlined three priorities for advancing the partnership: strengthening existing cooperation frameworks, recognizing the link between security and economic prosperity, and ensuring balanced strategic relations.

He said Gulf-European ties already had established foundations, including a 1989 cooperation agreement, the first GCC-EU summit in Brussels, joint action plans and regular political and security dialogues. The focus should be on reinforcing these mechanisms and giving them greater political momentum rather than creating new structures.

He also called for predictable rules, fair market access, easier movement for people and businesses, and closer consultation on policies affecting both sides.

European Mediterranean countries, he said, could play a greater role in strengthening GCC relations within EU institutions, helping position the Gulf as a key partner in security, stability and economic development.

Albudaiwi said the historical ties and shared interests between the Gulf and Mediterranean provided a strong foundation for a more secure and prosperous future, but political will was needed to turn closer relations into concrete results.

World.title: Spanish PM Sanchez admits mistakes, defends record amid far-right surge before vote
World.content:
MADRID: Spain’s Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged making “mistakes” as he faced off with his main conservative rival in a key debate on Thursday before an election next week that could leave the far right on the cusp of power.

The pair clashed over the economy, housing, immigration, corruption, foreign policy, as well as policies toward women, repeatedly interrupting each other during the live televised showdown.

“My government has not been perfect, I have made mistakes. But I am also fully aware that we have always governed in the right direction,” Sanchez said at the outset.

Pointing to economic growth and employment figures, he argued Spain was in better shape than when he took power in 2018, a claim rejected by the leader of the mainstream right-wing Popular Party (PP), Alberto Nunez Feijoo.

“Having a job does not guarantee you can make ends meet. Having a job does not guarantee you can afford a home either. You have crushed the middle class,” he told Sanchez.

“The Spanish economy is posting growth figures, but many families are still having to perform financial gymnastics to make ends meet.”

Feijoo rattled off what he called the government’s failures, including soaring prices, high taxes and a housing crisis.

Graft cases

A darling of the international left for his clashes with US President Donald Trump and Israel, Sanchez has become a polarizing figure in Spain following eight years in power.

His Socialists trail in most polls to the PP, which is predicted to win the most seats on November 29 but without securing a majority.

That scenario could hand a decisive role to the ascendant far-right party Vox, the third-largest force in parliament which has already governed with the PP at the regional level.

Further complicating the situation for Sanchez is the weakness of other leftist parties whose support proved crucial to keep him in power after the last general election in 2023.

The PP won more seats in that vote, but Sanchez unexpectedly cut the gap in polling and stayed in power after cobbling together a motley alliance with left-wing and regional separatist parties.

Sanchez, who has made escaping seemingly hopeless positions a hallmark of his career, believes he can defy the predictions again.

He has sought to capitalize on anger over Spain’s housing crisis, which brought forward an election originally due in 2027 after the right voted down the government’s measures for tenants.

But Feijoo accused Sanchez of not doing enough to avoid the housing crunch and brought up corruption scandals that have affected his relatives and senior Socialists.

He also blamed Sanchez’s government for two high-speed train collisions this year that together killed 115 people.

“Spain deserves a respectable prime minister, and (Pedro Sanchez) is not one,” Feijoo said.

‘Problem for Europe’

Sanchez warned a PP-Vox coalition would roll back hard-won social rights and economic gains.

“We can do even better, because we will deliver greater social justice, better public services and greater prosperity,” Sanchez said.

He also defended his government’s more liberal approach to immigration, bucking a broader European trend toward tougher migration controls and stricter asylum policies.

In April, Spain approved a plan to grant legal status to hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants already living in the country, provided they meet residency and other requirements.

“You are a problem for Europe when it comes to immigration,” his rival retorted, recalling the migrant rush into the Spanish city of Ceuta on the northern coast of Africa in July.

The debate was the campaign’s only head-to-head encounter between the two main contenders.

Vox leader Santiago Abascal, who could take the far right into power for the first time since the end of General Francisco Franco’s dictatorship in 1975, has dismissed the match-up.

“I don’t know what they will debate tonight. I am the one who is missing for there to be a real difference of opinions,” he said earlier.

World.title: Alibaba defrauded shareholders by concealing ties to suspected spy in Nvidia scandal, lawsuit says
World.content:
NEW YORK: Shareholders on Thursday sued Alibaba in New York, accusing the Chinese e-commerce giant of defrauding them by concealing its ties to the suspected Chinese spy whose relationship with former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang contributed to his resignation last week.

According to a proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly and materially understating in ‌its 2024, ‌2025 and 2026 annual reports the risks that ​actual ‌or ⁠suspected ​export control violations ⁠could harm its business.

Shareholders cited Alibaba’s relationship with Megaspeed, a Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing gain access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, and whose executive Alice Huang had a relationship with Jensen Huang, who is not related to her.

The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14 percent over four days last week because of media reports on Alibaba’s ties to Alice Huang and ⁠Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had become Megaspeed’s “dominant” customer.

They attributed part ‌of the decline to a November ‌12 Reuters article that said Nvidia’s spy scandal ​could spur Washington to tighten restrictions ‌on Chinese AI companies’ remote use of advanced processors.

Alibaba did not immediately ‌respond to requests for comment. Eddie Wu, its chief executive, is also a defendant.

Nvidia itself faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations of lax oversight by its directors.

Wu said on Thursday that Alibaba remained on track for $100 billion ‌in external cloud revenue and a 20 percent EBITDA margin by 2030, despite US curbs on access to computing ⁠power that ⁠could affect the company’s products and services next year. The restrictions were imposed after Huang resigned from Nvidia.

In June, Alibaba sued the US government over being added to a blacklist of “Chinese military companies” that the Department of Defense linked to that country’s military.

Last month, a federal judge in California granted Alibaba an injunction barring the US government from denying Pentagon contracts to companies whose lobbyists also work with designated Chinese military companies.

Alibaba said that restriction caused its lobbyists to retreat because they feared losing other clients, and violated its First Amendment constitutional right to speak to and petition ​the government.

Thursday’s lawsuit by Alibaba ​shareholder Withida Bihan seeks unspecified damages for holders of Alibaba’s American depositary shares between May 23, 2024 and November 11, 2026.

World.title: California attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about disgraced former CEO, China ties
World.content:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia related ​to reports of former CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

“The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags,” Bonta said, adding that his office was examining whether Nvidia or Huang’s actions resulted in China ‌obtaining advanced chips ‌or confidential information, and if ​the ‌company ⁠misled investors ​and the ⁠public about the risk.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia’s actions violated California law, the attorney general’s office said.

Huang resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia ⁠employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to ‌determine the extent of ‌Alice Huang’s ties to China’s ​Ministry of State Security ‌and what information she may have passed to ‌Beijing, according to Reuters.

China has rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang.

Nvidia’s board has ruled out bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, despite a campaign ‌by employees and prominent technology figures, including Elon Musk, to reinstate him.

The ⁠US ⁠Securities and Exchange Commission is also reportedly probing Nvidia after Huang’s resignation.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday that the Trump administration had approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May this year, although it was unclear how many were ultimately shipped.

Nvidia said the approvals were subject to strict ​conditions and limited volumes ​and that it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

World.title: Judge tells prosecutors that terrorism case defendant can read violent religious passages
World.content:
NEW YORK: A federal judge told federal prosecutors Thursday that the government must permit a man jailed on terrorism charges access to religious materials describing an important figure in Muslim history even if passages advocate violence because similar violent texts in the Bible would never be banned from distribution in jails.

Judge Colleen McMahon made the statement as she presided over a hearing where Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, repeatedly tried to speak directly to her, leading US marshals to usher him quickly out of the courtroom at one point.

His lawyer, Andrew Dalack, said the government had denied Al-Saadi access to a biography of a man who lived 1,300 years ago and who McMahon described as a “seminal figure in Muslim” history.

Assistant US Attorney Jeffrey Coyle said the materials sent by Al-Saadi’s family contained passages that “justifies the blood revenge of enemies.”

McMahon stopped just short of issuing a ruling from the bench that religious texts do not pose a threat to the special administrative measure that severely limit Al-Saadi’s communications with the outside world. But she made her opinions clear.

“Excuse me,” she said, interrupting the prosecutor at one point. “There are passages in the Bible that could be read the same way.”

She cited “statements of immense violence” in the Bible, including the book of Joshua calling for killings “in the most vicious and disgusting way.”

The judge also said she didn’t understand why he’d been denied newspaper articles about support for him in Egypt and a demonstration carried out on his behalf.

Al-Saadi was charged last week in a rewritten indictment accusing him of trying to pass secret messages to Iranian operatives planning an attack on a British air base used by the US Air Force.

The superseding indictment alleged that he had a role plotting to attack the Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, in western England, even though he’d been arrested last spring. A group of men were detained on Sept. 27 on suspected explosives and terrorism offenses after three suspicious vans were spotted traveling toward the air base where US bombers are stationed.

Prosecutors say that Al-Saadi used coded language in phone and video calls to his mother and sister in Iraq to pass messages encouraging associates to carry out the air base bombing.

Dalack said his client did not do it.

“Mr. Al-Saadi denies that he’s using coded messages in communications with his family. If you look at what the government points to, it relies on pure surmise and speculation,” Dalack said.

Coyle said the government is not letting Al-Saadi have any more calls with his family.

According to the indictment, Al-Saadi was among three men who conspired together to use a network of contacts in the United Kingdom to commit terror attacks on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network, which included the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Kata’ib Hizballah.

In June, Al-Saadi pleaded not guilty to charges that he plotted at least 18 attacks in Europe in retaliation for the US and Israel’s war with Iran. He called himself a “prisoner of war.” He has been held without bail since.

Both Kata’ib Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps have been designated by the US government as foreign terrorist organizations. US prosecutors say Al-Saadi was a Kata’ib Hizballah commander.

Al-Saadi tried several times at Thursday’s hearing to speak directly to McMahon. Speaking through an Arabic interpreter, his first outburst came as he was being arraigned on the new allegations.

Asked to enter a plea, he said: “I’m a statesmen. not a businessman.” Then, he added: “I’m innocent of the charge.”

“I’ll take that as a not-guilty plea,” the judge responded.

During another outburst, McMahon told him: “It’s really not a good idea for you to talk to me today.”

Shortly afterward, he was hurried out of court by marshals as he began shouting toward the judge that he wanted his lawyers replaced by attorneys that his family will retain.

After his current lawyers met with him, Dalack said Al-Saadi had decided to return to jail rather than come back into the courtroom.

“He’s obviously quite frustrated,” Dalack said.

The judge said she was adjourning proceedings in his case to give his family time to search for lawyers. She set a Feb. 10 date for him to return to court.

World.title: Anthropic surges in market debut after biggest IPO on record, despite fears that AI is running amok
World.content:
NEW YORK: The artificial intelligence giant Anthropic rose sharply Thursday after making the biggest public stock offering ever, at one point surpassing $2 trillion in value, despite anxiety about an AI bubble and fear that the technology threatens lives and livelihoods.

Its shares shot higher as trading began and held on to much of those gains to close up 17 percent at $97.17. The initial offering overtook SpaceX as the largest IPO in history.

Anthropic’s initial offer of $82 per share was surprisingly high given the investor worries that ratcheted up even more recently following the stunning ouster of AI’s chief promoter, the CEO of Nvidia, in a possible Chinese spying scandal. Anthropic had earlier set a lower price range between $70 and $78 per share.

“It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co. “The pricing shows strong demand among investors.”

For his part, Anthropic’s CEO tried to dampen worry about AI’s threat to society.

“If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same,” Dario Amodei said.

The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude AI tool offered 980 million shares to the public, which at the $83 per share price translated into proceeds of $81 billion.

IPO offers a way to raise money without going deeper into debt

In addition to recent market jitters, Anthropic’s debut sale had to overcome fears of a potential regulatory crackdown next year by the Democratic-led Congress and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public. Anthropic rival OpenAI decided to postpone its initial offering until next year.

The company, trading under the ticker symbol ANT, also faces big financial challenges ahead.

Anthropic already has taken on $6.2 billion in debt, which it acknowledges in financial filings is “substantial.” Adding to the strain, the company is unprofitable, at least under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to pay interest and principal are limited.

While the company showed ample cash in its last financial report, it would have likely run through it quickly given its outsize spending plans. In the same financial report, the company said it had signed leases and other deals requiring it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure in the coming years, including $70 billion in the next 12 months.

Such massive spending by AI companies, comparable to the Gilded Age splurge on railroads, has scared lenders, helping to push borrowing rates high recently.

With the IPO, though, Anthropic will now have enormous resources to accelerate its expansion without taking on more debt. In addition to the cash from public investors, the company also planned to sell $26 billion in shares in a private sale Thursday to bring the total raised to $107 billion — an impressive haul for a business not yet six years old.

The offering will also allow its employees to sell vested stock, making many of them millionaires overnight — and adding billions of dollars to the fortunes of CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic President Daniela Amodei.

AI industry faces concerns about data centers, a possible bubble and regulations

Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with OpenAI. But both companies have plenty of other competitors, including Google, startups in the US and China and SpaceX, which has an AI business.

Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX’s AI division have all lost more money than they’ve made because of the huge costs associated with building AI. That has fueled growing concerns about a bubble forming in the sector.

Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned, AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the Internet within months.

Amid mounting fears, the regulatory environment could change for Anthropic once the new Congress is in session. Newly elected Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry as a backlash unfolds against data centers. And two big states offering incentives for data centers, Texas and Georgia, just elected Democratic governors who have vowed to stop new construction.

In his comments Thursday, Amodei also touted a range of positive uses for AI, noting that Claude already is helping scientists do quicker research and that the technology could help accelerate that progress in the future.

“Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox and polio history for most of the world,” he said, “but progress in other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families.”

He also pointed to Claude’s use across companies, nonprofits and government services. “I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future,” he said.

Adding to the pressure to go public was the possibility that demand for AI shares could drop or even collapse. Investors have become anxious about the massive financing needs of the sector, and several tech companies have pulled IPO plans recently.

Market valuation for AI companies is going to be “up and down for many years to come, but more up than down,” said Rich Lesser, the global chair and former CEO of Boston Consulting Group.

“Exactly what the flow of that will be, it’s very hard to predict,” Lesser said Tuesday in an interview with The Associated Press at the Semafor Silicon Valley & the World forum. “There’s no question what Anthropic and OpenAI and Google and a number of the other players in this industry have done is pretty remarkable.”

World.title: Kushner says he believes Russia is ‘comfortable’ with NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine
World.content:
BERLIN: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday he believes Russia is “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for postwar Ukraine, while Kyiv’s European allies expressed concerns about President Donald Trump’s meeting in China with the Kremlin leader.

President Vladimir Putin, meanwhile, vowed to retaliate against Ukraine for the “seriously damage” it caused with three aerial attacks this week on the vital Kerch Bridge, which links occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland.

“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China, where he attended the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

Kushner and fellow US envoy Steve Witkoff were in Berlin to reassure nearly 40 European leaders about Trump’s discussions on ending the nearly 5-year-old war at his historic trilateral talks with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Ukraine has long sought entry into NATO, particularly for its common defense guarantee under the alliance’s Article 5, in which an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. It was not immediately clear what form potential security guarantees would take, and whether Russia and Ukraine would ultimately accept them.

Trump signals support for security guarantee for Ukraine

The Berlin meeting was convened to explore Ukraine’s postwar security arrangements with Kyiv’s European backers. President Volodymyr Zelensky wants to ensure that Russia doesn’t invade again, while Moscow wants to keep the NATO military alliance away from its borders.

“I think we’ve gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5,” Kushner said. “And I think that that comes with at least what the Russians are saying, which is their intention is when this war is over to not have another war in the future.”

Kushner said Trump is “open” to an Article 5-like security guarantee for Ukraine, although “obviously it has to be in America’s interest to do that. And we also have to make sure that it’s part of a broader security package.”

He stressed that Trump wants to make a deal with Europe “by his side,” and is not looking to impose a unilateral agreement.

“Any deal we do will be in close consultation with Ukraine and with Europe. And that’s something that he also asked us to come here today and reassure people in that regard,” said Kushner, who is Trump’s son-in-law.

He and Witkoff have led Trump administration efforts to end the war that followed Russia’s all-out invasion of Ukraine. The most recent talks in Abu Dhabi last week yielded no major breakthrough.

Trump called into the Berlin talks following his meeting with Putin, according to Kushner.

The Kerch Bridge is a symbol of Russia’s hold on Crimea

Thursday’s Berlin meeting came hours after the latest attack on the Kerch Bridge by Ukraine. The strikes have seriously damaged the 19-kilometer (12-mile) bridge over the Kerch Strait that links the Black and Azov seas. The span is vital to sustaining Russia’s military operations.

The bridge is a potent reminder of Russia’s illegal annexation of the Crimean Peninsula and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

Train traffic stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Putin as he met in China with Xi and Trump, as well as to undermine Russia’s argument that its victory is inevitable.

In China, Putin insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered it closed to carrying military hardware or ammunition.

Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” but vowed to rebuild it. The rail section, which runs parallel to the road, is believed to be stronger in order to bear the greater weight of cargo transport.

Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said Russia will need to reroute fuel and ammunition supplies over land, where “our drones are waiting for the cargo.”

Attacks kill 4 civilians in Russia, 2 in Ukraine, officials say

The Russian Defense Ministry said Thursday its defenses intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.

A Ukrainian attack on Russia’s Saratov region killed three people and wounded two others, local Gov. Roman Busargin said, and a drone killed a woman traveling by bicycle with her 8-year-old grandson in the Bryansk region, Gov. Egor Kovalchuk said.

Ukrainian authorities said that Russia launched anti-ship missiles and 98 drones at Ukraine, with hits recorded at 18 locations. Explosions and sirens rang out across Kyiv during the day, and the Dutch and Austrian embassies sustained minor damage, officials said.

Two people, including a 44-year-old woman, were killed and at least 23 people, including a 12-year-old boy, were reported wounded as Russian strikes caused damage in 12 regions.

Russia’s bigger army hopes to exhaust Ukraine on the front line through sheer weight of numbers in terms of soldiers, armor and weapons. But Kyiv’s defenses are largely holding the Russians back, sapping Russian momentum with the help of drones that quickly choke off troop advances.

Russia has resorted to strategic bombing to wear down Ukraine’s resistance, placing special emphasis on knocking out power ahead of winter, while Kyiv’s domestically developed long-range drones and missiles have struck deep inside Russia, often targeting its oil refineries.

Kyiv fears Trump and Putin may try to decide Ukraine’s fate

In China, Trump called Putin “my friend.” The American president’s relationship with Zelensky has soured recently, although the question of US support for Ukraine could be raised by Democrats who will take control of Congress in January after their wins in the midterm elections.

European leaders have tried to isolate Putin diplomatically and have heavily sanctioned the Russian economy as they fear being sidelined by Trump’s direct talks with Putin.

Kushner said that, in his talks with Putin and Xi, Trump “sent a very strong message to both of them on the desire for peace and would like to engage both of them very aggressively to get there.”

He deferred to Trump on giving any details of the “private discussions,” but added: “I believe he also came away believing that peace is achievable and we need to all work together to try and achieve it.”

Putin said in Shenzhen that the Kremlin is not against European participation in talks, but “we need to understand with what Europe will come to these negotiations.” The Kremlin has proposed to European officials through diplomatic channels to come to Moscow “to determine their position,” Putin said, without elaborating. No date has been set.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to say which European officials had been invited or whether Moscow had received a response, Russian state news agency Tass reported.

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: Iraq studies issuing electronic dinar to expand financial inclusion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is investigating an electronic dinar as a digital extension of the current national currency to modernize payments, increase financial inclusion, and lessen reliance on physical cash.

Prime Minister’s financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Saleh highlighted the initiative in remarks to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Wednesday, though no launch date, technical specifications, or formal issuance decision have been announced.

The electronic dinar will serve as a digital representation equal in value to the physical paper dinar rather than a new currency issue. It will not automatically generate new liquidity but will improve the management and circulation of existing funds.

According to the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), approximately 102 trillion dinars ($67.38 billion)—nearly 92 percent of all currency issued—is held outside the formal banking system.

The purpose of a digital currency is to direct the financial reserves into formal savings, lending, and profitable ventures.

Moving transactions onto official digital channels will help curb unregulated financial dealings, reduce cash-printing costs, and align Iraq with the CBI’s financial inclusion strategy.

The digital dinar plan is different from suggestions to eliminate zeros from the physical currency.

Although the CBI has expanded bank cards, digital wallets, and points of sale, it has not yet declared a formal launch date or technical introduction timetable.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: 'Everybody's got an opinion': Rahul Gandhi explains why he is called a youth leader at 56
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader

responded to being called a 'youth leader' despite being 56, saying age should not define youth. In a conversation, Rahul said remaining curious and never being afraid to ask questions, even those considered unusual or ridiculous, was what kept a person young.

During a conversation at the University of Chicago, Rahul said he had never accepted the idea that certain questions should not be asked and believed curiosity across subjects was what defined youth.

"Look, everybody's got an opinion, okay? So somebody will say, I'm a youth leader. Somebody will say, I'm an old people's leader. Somebody will say something else. I mean, it's fine. Everybody is allowed to have a perspective," Rahul said.



Responding to a question about why young people identify with him, Rahul Gandhi said he had been encouraged from an early age to remain curious and ask questions across different subjects.

"But I was taught when I was small to always be curious and to not have boundaries on your curiosity. So to ask questions in all spheres, you know, ask a question about geopolitics, ask a question about women's health, ask a question about animals, ask a question about pretty much anything," he said.





He added that society gradually places restrictions on people's curiosity as they grow older, encouraging them to focus on conventional measures of success.

"So what society is going to try and tell you as you progress is that there are certain questions you can't ask, and there's certain questions that you just shouldn't ask. And there is a set of questions that you can ask," Rahul Gandhi said.

"You know, you can ask, how do I make money? You can ask, how do I own a big house? You can ask, how do I do well at work as adults? But then there's a whole bunch of questions you're not allowed to ask.

I never bought into that."

He cited the example of his former mathematics tutor, whom he met for breakfast and learnt was pursuing a master's degree in his 60s.

Rahul Gandhi said people should continue asking questions, including those that others might consider unusual or uncomfortable.

"And to me, that is what you have right now that you should never lose, never be scared of asking the most ridiculous questions, questions that people just will not ask themselves.

And that's what youth is. So maybe that's why they say I'm a youth leader," he said.

The conversation also turned to generational change in political leadership, particularly in the United States, where younger leaders from different political camps are emerging.

Asked about the youth movement in American politics, Rahul Gandhi said he had noticed a shift in how Western leaders approached international affairs.

He recalled that leaders he encountered early in his political career had a broader understanding of global developments.

"I noticed something in leadership in the West. Right. And I noticed when I first came into politics, the leaders had a pretty good understanding of. Of the rest of the world. There was a decent sense. I remember having a conversation with Mr. Tony Blair, and I was like, okay, he gets Afghanistan or he has a sense of India," he said.

However, Gandhi said he later encountered leaders who appeared more focused on domestic issues and had limited understanding of developments in other countries.

"And then suddenly in the middle, I found a group of leaders who were focused completely on what was going on in their country. And they would come, and I'm not saying one particular country, they'd come. And it was obvious that they didn't have the grounding or understanding of our stuff," he said.

Rahul Gandhi also referred to Russian President Vladimir Putin while discussing leaders with a broader understanding of geopolitics.

"At risk of getting into trouble. Mr. Putin has one of the most profound geopolitical minds that I have come across. He can talk in massive sweep about these type of things. And I think that was the thing that. That struck me. There was a moving inwards of Western leadership," he said.

He added that Western leaders had increasingly focused on domestic issues rather than developments beyond their borders.

"you know, looking inside and focusing on the home more than outside. That's just an experience I had. I don't know if I'm correct or wrong," Congress leader said.

He also suggested that some younger leaders were beginning to show a wider interest in international affairs.

"But the reason I said that is that some of these young guys, they seem to be re looking at the outside world. They seem to be having now a vision of a bigger scope than earlier," he said.

World.title: SC allows German mother to take child to Singapore, grants dad visitation rights
World.content:
A bench of Justices N K Singh and N V Anjaria said it was seeking to protect the childâs autonomy

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Faced with a "piquant situation" in deciding a custody battle over a four-year-old child of unwed parents of different nationalities - a Singapore-based German mother who works for TikTok and an Indian father who runs a legal firm in Delhi - SC examined their proposals to care for the child and allowed the mother to take him to Singapore, granting visitation rights to the father.A bench of Justices N K Singh and N V Anjaria said it was seeking to protect the child's autonomy, which had been jeopardised by parents' bickering. It said the mother's proposal appeared realistic and beneficial to the child.After their relationship fell apart, the mother alleged the father was denying her access to and custody of the child, and sought the court's permission to take him to Singapore for his education.SC held that the mother had a better prima facie claim to custody and that the balance of convenience favoured her. It said the child could suffer irreparable injury if interim custody was not granted, as the mother had a more concrete plan for his well-being.Addressing the father's apprehension that she might not return or cooperate with proceedings in a Delhi family court, it directed her to obtain a mirror order from a Singapore court within three weeks. After filing it, she must deposit Rs 1 crore with the SC registry, to be kept in a fixed deposit for two years or until the guardianship petition is disposed of.

World.title: ED didn't follow norms, says court, gives relief to businessman in AJL case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A special MP/MLA court in Delhi on Nov 14 ordered cancellation of a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against one Dinesh Pandey of Lamore Hotel Pvt Ltd, the company which had allegedly paid Rs 10 crore to Associated Journals Ltd, the publisher of Congress mouthpiece National Herald, now controlled by Sonia Gandhi-led Young Indian.

The NBW was issu

in 2022 after Pandey failed to appear for questioning before the ED on repeated summonses in the National Herald related money laundering case. He has been out of the country ever since. Later, in 2024, he moved an application seeking cancellation of the NBW. Pandey was earlier arrested in Nov 2020 in the bike bot scam but was out on bail.

While cancelling the NBW, the court held that ED had not followed procedure as prescribed under CrPC and Sec 19 of PMLA.



"The prosecution should record the reasons in writing the compelling circumstances for issuance of NBWs and when arrest is made, such grounds should also be disclosed to such a person so apprehended, which is again a mandatory requirement of Section 41A of CrPC/35 BNSS".

"At the time of moving of the application seeking issuance of NBWs against Dinesh Pandey, which resulted into impugned order dated 11.11.2022, there was non-compliance of the mandatory procedural requirement...It appears that correct picture was not apprised to the Court," special judge Prashant Kumar noted in his order, cancelling the NBWs.

World.title: Women should get 33% quota in legal profession, says SC judge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Holding that formal equality between genders alone may not be sufficient to secure meaningful representation of women in institutions where "historical exclusion has shaped the composition", Supreme Court judge Justice B V Nagarathna said that reservation should be provided to women in the legal profession on the lines of seats reserved for women in panchayats, municipalities and legislatures.

She said that one-third of the seats in the legal profession be reserved for them.

Referring to the 73rd and 74th Constitutional amendments on local bodies and the 106th Amendment for LS and state assemblies, Justice Nagarathna said the same principle must inform the legal profession. She advocated one-third reservation for women lawyers on govt panels, including those representing public sector undertakings, and in legal aid.

Delivering the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lec-ture at Somerville College, University of Oxford, on 'Progress of Women's Rights in India', she said equality must extend from recruitment and training to promotion and leadership.

She said women's safety, access to justice & economic equality remained concerns. Despite laws recognising equal remuneration, maternity protection and workforce participation, unpaid domestic and care work continued to place a disproportionate burden on women.

World.title: BJP cites Moily remark to claim Congress tried to 'frame' PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

leader M Veerappa Moily has claimed

would have gone to jail when he was CM of Gujarat but the probe against him was stalled by some Congress members when the party was in office; comments cited by

as vindication of its charge that Modi was being targeted as part of political vendetta.

Moily's comment acquires significance in light of speculation in political circles before 2014 LS polls that Modi and

Amit Shah

could be arrested in Ishrat Jahan case.

"The mask has completely fallen off," BJP spokesman Sudhanshu Trivedi said, adding that Moily's statement suggested that investigating agencies and judicial processes were "completely sidelined" under Congress govt, which tried to "frame" Modi, and demanded a response from the opposition party.



Speaking at the release of Sonia Gandhi's memoir at Congress office in Bengaluru, Moily said Shah had gone to jail and was externed, and claimed that he would not have become the powerful home minister that he is now. Shah was arrested in Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case. He was later discharged.

Moily, a cabinet minister in UPA govt, said, "The next would have been Modi to go inside (jail). The investigation against Narendra Modi was stalled.





(By) our own govt, not because of Manmohan Singh (then PM) but some other leaders. We are suffering because of that today."

BJP said Moily's remarks made it clear that Congress tried to "frame" Modi and Shah and all allegations levelled against them back then were "politically motivated".

World.title: In Tokyo, India and Japan press for multipolar world
World.content:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh and EAM S Jaishankar with their Japan counterparts, Koizumi Shinjiro and Motegi Toshimitsu, in Tokyo

India and Japan Thursday voiced concerns about the growing tendency to weaponise connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares, with external affairs minister S Jaishankar warning that these had direct implications on national security.He was speaking after the 4th India-Japan 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministerial Meeting in Tokyo that saw both sides reaffirming their opposition to unilateral attempts to change the status quo by coercion in the Indo-Pacific region. Unlike the joint statement, a Japanese readout said the ministers discussed the situation in East and South China Sea, along with West Asia and Ukraine.Jaishankar and defence minister Rajnath Singh held the 2+2 dialogue with their counterparts, Motegi Toshimitsu and Koizumi Shinjiro, days after the Quad summit in the Philippines. According to Jaishankar, the big picture that India-Japan cooperation seeks to support is a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world, with the two countries acting as strong proponents of reformed multilateralism.He said in his media remarks that concerns about connectivity and chokepoints had grown in the light of experiences in the Gulf. âEnsuring that maritime trade, which is at the heart of global commerce, functions smoothly is imperative,â he said.Both sides committed to strengthening an international order that was free, open and based on the rule of law, respect for national sovereignty and territorial integrity and peaceful resolution of disputes. In remarks aimed at China, the ministers reiterated concerns over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions and non-market policies that result in overcapacity.Alluding to concerns about a possible US retreat, Jaishankar said the strategic landscape of the Indo-Pacific remained complex and old assumptions may not hold true. âEach one of us will have to make a greater contribution to global good. These are done through initiatives and activities which are national, bilateral or with like-minded partners,â he said.

World.content:
on Thursday said those excluded from the draft Delhi electoral roll must utilise the available 11 days to file enumeration forms, Forms 6 or 8 to register as voters and said it would not hesitate to extend the Nov 30 deadline for inclusion of voters if it finds it necessary on taking stock of the situation on Dec 2.

Referring to its Oct 28 order that made EC extend the Oct 30 deadline by a month for registration of names which were excluded from the post-enumeration draft electoral roll, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana told petitionerâs counsel Prashant Bhushan that when the time comes, the issues raised would be adjudicated.

Right now, the priority is to ensure all eligible voters are included, it said.



On Dec 2, we will examine extending deadline to have voters included in the voters list," the bench said and asked EC counsel D S Naidu to give details by then of the number of enumeration forms, Forms 6 and 8 received and approved by the EC during the one-month period between Oct 30 and Nov 30.

World.title: PM uses GTA VI launch to take dig at Congress
World.content:
PM

Thursday tapped into the palpable excitement over the launch of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI, the latest version of the popular action video game, to highlight the changes India has seen under his govt over 12 years since GTA's last version was released in 2013, when Congress-led UPA govt was in office.

"India is playing a whole new game," Modi said, sharing colourful graphics styled around the game's striking visual appeal to make a point about positive changes ushered in by his govt. He has often used the buzz over aspects of popular culture to score a political point over his rivals and connect with a wider audience.

"Between GTA V and VI, here's how India upgraded," an illustration said. From being among "fragile five" economies to the world's fastest-growing, from 2.82 GW of solar capacity to 175 GW, and from 20% railway electrification to 99.6%, it added. PM said India now has 440 space startups, compared to "Sorry! no result found" in the earlier period. Extreme poverty fell from 27% to 2.6%, while internet cost dropped from Rs 308/ GB to Rs 7.51/GB even as the network upgraded from 3G to 5G.

GTA VI has an Indian connection as well. Developed by Rockstar Games, a part of the video game was reportedly built at its Indian division based in Bengaluru.

World.title: Time to protect eroding coastlines
World.content:
For Professor B.S.R. Reddy, who retired from the Department of Meteorology and Oceanography at Andhra University, reaching the sea from the Beach Road in the early 1960s meant walking at least half a kilometre over high dunes—an exciting journey up one sandhill and down another. Residing at the Pithapuram Beach Hostels as a student, opposite the site where the INS Kursura Submarine Museum now stands, he recalls hearing the crashing waves from the road amidst the shouts of fellow students playing football on the sand, even though the sea itself was hidden from view. Today, he says, there are “no beaches” along stretches of that road, and the waves strike it directly.

Beyond the disappearing stretches of sand, the consequences of coastal erosion are being felt not only by those who depend on the sea for their livelihoods, but also by the State, which is steadily losing land to the encroaching sea.

For instance, earlier this month the seaward edge of the beach road near the museum had been cut away, with rubble and boulders strewn across the sand below. Near RK Beach, waves had eroded a sand bank beneath a row of coconut palms, exposing the bases of trees and cable conduits.

This loss is also documented in the Shoreline Change Atlas of Andhra Pradesh, published in February 2024 by the National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR), under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences. Using satellite imagery, the agency mapped 1,027.58 km of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline between 1990 and 2022. It found that 31 per cent (318.96 km) is eroding, 24.9 per cent is stable, and 44 per cent is gaining sand—with about 91.6 km falling in the “high erosion” category, losing more than five metres a year.

According to the atlas, the losses are concentrated in the delta districts. In Kakinada, 52.8 per cent of the coast is eroding, followed by West Godavari at 52.5 per cent, and Krishna at 43.8 per cent. It mentions that coastal port district Visakhapatnam lies somewhere in between. Of its 70.61 km of coast, 25.9 per cent is eroding, mostly at a rate of 0.5m to 3m a year; 51.3 per cent is stable and 22.8 per cent is gaining sand. The district map identifies one erosion hotspot at Pedanagamayyapalem near Bheemunipatnam.

World.title: FSSAI licences suspended of two Karachi Bakery units in Hyderabad, four meat outlets over food safety violations
World.content:
The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) has suspended the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) licences of six establishments, including two units linked to Karachi Bakery in Hyderabad, following inspections that exposed serious food safety violations.

The establishments include Karachi INC in Srinagar Colony, Karachi Bakery Pearl Private Limited at Gaganpahad, Watan Traders in Musheerabad, Punjab Fish Company in Secunderabad, Hi Protein on SD Road and SM SEA Corporation in Uppal. All six have been directed to immediately stop business operations in the interest of public health.

The action was part of a special enforcement drive conducted on Thursday (November 19, 2026) by 11 teams comprising Food Safety Officers and police personnel. The teams inspected 15 meat retail and processing units and four Karachi Bakery manufacturing units across Hyderabad and its outskirts.

The violations detected at units associated with Karachi Bakery include pest infestation, cobwebs, rat droppings, rusty baking trays, defective machinery, unclean refrigerators in the cake section, cleaning chemicals stored alongside food articles and clogged kitchen drains. Officials seized 1,012 kg of packed food products worth ₹4.34 lakh from the Gaganpahad unit.

The violations at other four establishments, which were meat shops, include slaughtering waste found discarded or stored in unhygienic conditions, clogged drains in its processing areas, raw fish and prawns exposed to flies, expired frozen prawns were found in storage, dead flies inside a freezer.

Separately, TG SAFE seized approximately 1,672 kg of food articles worth ₹6.59 lakh during the inspections and ordered five meat retail and processing establishments to shut down for operating without FSSAI licences and maintaining unhygienic conditions. They include Anand Mutton and Chicken Point at Shankarmat in Nallakunta, Salman KGN Poultry and New Decent Meat Chicken and Fish Shop at Erragadda, Protein Foods on SP Road in Secunderabad and AP Fisheries Fish Stall at Goutham Nagar Road in Malkajgiri.

Improvement notices will be issued to Watan Fresh Mart in Musheerabad and Metro Cash and Carry India Limited at Uppal, directing them to rectify the deficiencies. The establishments will be reinspected to verify compliance.

Additionally, show-cause notices will also be issued to 10 establishments, including Metro Cash and Carry outlets at Gaganpahad, Moosapet and Suchitra X Road, Sai Baba Inc (Karachi Bakery) at M.J. Market in Goshamahal and Licious at Kistapur village in Medchal mandal, along with the five establishments ordered to shut down. Further action, including penalties, will be initiated based on the violations, TG SAFE said.

World.title: Delhi court asks for action taken report on sexual harassment complaint against ACP despite police’s closure claim in Supreme Court
World.content:
A Delhi court has sought a detailed account of the police action on the complaint filed by a journalist who accused Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat of groping her while she was covering the detention of student leader Neha Bora at Jantar Mantar on October 3.

On November 16, the Delhi Police told the Supreme Court that sexual assault cases by three women journalists during the anti-SIR protests in the Capital in October were ‘closed’, while in a fourth case, no video evidence was found to warrant further proceedings.

In an order dated November 3, accessed by The Hindu, Judicial Magistrate First Class Kautuk Bhardwaj of the Patiala House Courts directed the Station House Officer (SHO) concerned to submit an action taken report (ATR), answering five specific questions about the complaint and the subsequent police inquiry.

The Court asked the SHO to state whether the complaint had been received at the police station and, if so, what action had been taken. It also sought details on whether the investigation or inquiry established the commission of any cognisable offence against the accused and whether any action followed. If an FIR had been registered, the police were asked to provide its status and the progress of the investigation. If no cognisable offence had been made out, the SHO was required to clarify whether the complainant had been informed of the decision.

The Court directed that the response be filed “point-wise”, addressing each of its queries and detailing the action taken on the complaint before the complainant approached the Court.

The Court also directed the SHO to take all necessary steps within three days of receiving the order to preserve the relevant CCTV footage and other digital evidence, including body-camera footage. The compliance report on the preservation of the evidence is to be filed within a week. The matter is listed for December 1 for the filing of the ATR.

The journalist had lodged a complaint at the Parliament Street police station. The complaint, along with three other similar complaints by journalists, was transferred to the Crime Branch for inquiry on October 4.

In its affidavit before the Supreme Court, the Delhi Police said the four complaints of sexual harassment could not be independently corroborated. It maintained that two of the journalists did not wish to pursue their complaints, while the third did not join the police inquiry despite attempts to contact her. In the fourth case, the police said that examining CCTV footage, video recordings and witnesses present at the place of incident did not prima facie reveal any act of sexual harassment warranting further proceedings, including registration of an FIR. “The specific allegations could not be corroborated, and all the allegations levelled in the complaint stood negated,” the document read.

In a conversation with The Hindu, the journalist said after an initial round of questioning at the Crime Branch office in Prashant Vihar on October 8, she was questioned at least three more times over video calls.

Her counsel, advocate Saimon Farooqui, said the complainant was also taken to the protest ground with police personnel and asked to identify the precise location where the alleged incident occurred. She identified the spot, he added.

Mr. Farooqui said that after the 14-day period within which the police were expected to conclude the preliminary inquiry had elapsed, the complainant approached the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) seeking registration of an FIR. When there was no response or action, she moved the magistrate’s court.

On October 27, she received a notice from the investigating officer, dated October 22, informing her that the complaint had been closed as the allegations could not be corroborated.

“The notice stated that the police had examined the available evidence and witnesses. But this was way after the 14-day window,” Mr. Farooqui said.

“The refusal to register an FIR despite disclosure of a cognisable offence of sexual assault against the ACP was hardly surprising. After all, expecting the Delhi Police to investigate its own senior officer is perhaps expecting too much, especially when it was quick to register a counterblast FIR under the SC/ST Act against the complainant to settle personal scores. The wheels of justice are now in motion with an application under Section 175(3) of the BNSS. This case warrants not just an FIR, but the ACP’s immediate suspension and prosecution followed by conviction,” Mr. Farooqui said.

In its affidavit, the Delhi Police maintained that there were no strict rules for only women police personnel to handle women during such operations, arguing that the presence or involvement of male officers could not, by itself, be construed as misconduct.

The police also defended their approach to journalists covering the protests. The affidavit stated that the Supreme Court’s October 11 direction that journalists, lawyers and other professionals should not be hindered while discharging their professional duties did not extend to reel-makers and social media influencers.

AAP calls out Delhi police

Meanwhile, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday (November 19, 2026) criticised the Delhi Police over its handling of four sexual harassment complaints against ACP Vivek Bhagat.

AAP state president Saurabh Bharadwaj alleged that the Delhi Police closed three of the four cases, citing the complainants’ unwillingness or failure to pursue them.

He alleged that in the fourth case, involving a woman journalist, the police told the Court that they had found no video evidence of sexual harassment, despite journalists having staged a two-day protest outside the police station demanding an FIR against the ACP.

“Prime Minister Modi should be ashamed; he should be utterly disgraced. Even if he does not have children or a daughter of his own, he should at least think about someone else’s daughter. The police are saying that the incident was not captured on CCTV, and therefore, even the fourth woman journalist’s complaint has been placed under suspicion and her FIR has not been registered,” Mr. Bharadwaj said.

World.title: U.S. religious freedom panel says ‘India targeting minorities in voter roll revisions’
World.content:
India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities ‌during a voter list revision that struck off tens of millions ​of names nationwide, a U.S. panel on religious freedom said on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026).

“The Indian gov’t is targeting Muslim citizens by removing them from voter rolls, calling them ‘foreigners,’ and now illegally deporting them,” Asif Mahmood, the chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, ‌said in a statement.

India’s voter list revision removed 130 million names, roughly the population of Mexico, in the largest deletion of voters in the ‌country’s history.

Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims, India’s largest minority, who ‌have ⁠faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime ⁠Minister Narendra Modi took power in 2014.

The Election Commission of India says it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue ​appeals.

The revision has become entangled with ‌a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner.

“The Indian government’s expulsion of its own citizens based on their Muslim faith is a shocking ‌escalation of tactics that target religious minorities,” said Gene Mills, a commissioner ​on the U.S. panel.

Mr. Mills urged the State Department to designate India as a “country of particular concern.”

USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding. Washington has not acted on its recent recommendations on India.

The Ministry of External Affairs has cast USCIRF as biased. New Delhi has repeatedly dismissed such criticism and called it interference in the country’s internal affairs. The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

The voter roll revisions sparked protests in recent weeks, with opposition groups and student demonstrators saying the revisions affected those unlikely to vote for the BJP. Rights experts condemned India’s crackdown on the protests.

U.S. ‌Secretary of State Marco Rubio said last month the issue was a “domestic political matter” and ​Washington would not comment on it.

UN experts and human rights groups say abuse of minorities has risen under Mr. Modi.

They point to rising hate ⁠speech, a religion-based citizenship law that the UN calls “fundamentally discriminatory,” the demolition of Muslim-owned properties, and anti-conversion legislation that challenges freedom of belief.

Civil rights advocates have also been critical of the treatment of Muslims in the U.S. while noting a rise in Islamophobia ​in recent years and documenting escalating anti-Muslim rhetoric from Republicans during election campaigns.

World.title: COP 31: Nations still seeking deeper fossil fuel cuts as climate summit enters final day
World.content:
Negotiators entering the final day of this year's United Nations climate talks in Turkiye are seeking meaningful commitments to address global warming amid warnings that only drastic cuts in fossil fuel emissions can avert its most catastrophic effects.

Friday (November 20, 2026) marks the official end of the two-week annual summit, which has so far largely failed to advance any big ideas to move away from fossil fuels — mainly coal, oil and gas — which are contributing to more intense and deadly heat waves, droughts, floods and other disasters.

A goal introduced this year to increase the share of electricity in total global energy consumption from roughly 21% to 35% by 2035, preferably from renewable energy, also would allow the use of coal and other fossil fuels.

And leaders from countries ravaged by climate change — mostly poorer, vulnerable countries that contributed little to the problem — say a UN fund to help them recover from climate disasters and adapt to a warmer world is not nearly large enough.

Top-emitting nations did not participate directly in this year's summit, complicating efforts. That includes the United States, the world's second-largest polluter after China and the largest polluter historically, which is absent for the second year in a row.

A report last week by the independent nonprofit Climate Action Tracker found that progress in slowing global warming has essentially stalled for the past five years. That means the world is sure to overshoot the goal set in the 2015 Paris Agreement of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

Without drastic reductions beyond what countries already have promised, the globe will end the century 2.6 degrees Celsius (4.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warmer than pre-industrial times, the report said.

World.title: Vizag Junior Literary Fest: Where young minds find their voice
World.content:
What happens when a weekend is spent reading stories, meeting one’s favourite authors and discovering new worlds through books, art and imagination? Hundreds of children in Visakhapatnam are set to find the answer at the Vizag Junior Literary Fest (VJLF). The excitement is as much about stories waiting to be discovered as it is about the friendships, conversations and creative experiences that come with them.

Returning for its seventh edition on November 21 and 22, the festival, organised by Lit Lantern Culture and Literature Society, promises a packed programme featuring 20 speakers and close to 100 sessions. With a fresh line-up of authors, illustrators, performers and artists, the two-day event hopes to turn literature into an immersive experience for children across age groups.

For festival directors Sonal Sarda, Priya Uppalapati and Sandhya Venugopal Godey, the larger idea is to create a space where children can connect with literature and, more importantly, with one another.

“The idea is to expose children to a wide spectrum of literature while encouraging genuine human connections in an increasingly device-driven world.
